chapters.title: Chapter 120: Beast Pavillion
paragraphs: As he scanned the basic text, he remembered something.
’Right...’
He closed the beginner manual, tucking it back into his pocket and then he tapped the interface hovering in his vision and opened his Lord Inventory.
When they had finished the novice trial and absorbed that massive wave of combat experience from the tide, the Blessed Land had officially hit Level 10.
The system had quietly rewarded him with a high-tier architectural construction bundle, unlocking several advanced blueprints that he hadn’t even bothered to look at yet.
With a flash of pixelated blue light, a long, heavy scroll of blue architectural paper materialized in his hand.
Reina and Aeliana watched in surprise as he unrolled the glowing blueprint across his forearms.
The paper didn’t just show drawings; it displayed live three-dimensional magical diagrams that shifted and pulsed with mana.
Silas’s eyes widened as he read the descriptions of the high-tier defensive formations unlocked in his bundle:
[Unlocked Blueprint:] Astral Ward Matrix - Tier 2
[Type:] Perimeter Defense / Area Denial.
[Materials Required:] 1,000 Refined Stone, 500 Star-Iron, 200 Void-Amethyst, 50 units of Liquid Starlight.

[Function:] Projects a thirty-foot dampening dome over designated structures. Reduces all incoming magical and physical projectile damage by 40%. Automatically fires high-velocity starlight lances at any hostile entity that breaches the outer wall without territorial authorization.
[Unlocked Blueprint:] Geothermal Mana Forge - Tier 2
[Type:] Industrial / Resource Refinement.
[Materials Required:] 800 Obsidian Blocks, 400 Deep-Earth Alloy, 100 Sun-Forge Topaz, 1 Heavy Smelting Core.

[Function:] A specialized furnace structure that taps directly into subterranean heat veins. Accelerates weapon forging speed by 50% and automatically purifies low-grade ore into high-density ingots without manual flux application.
[Unlocked Blueprint:] Umbral Frost-Turret Array - Tier 2
[Type:] Automated Fortification.
[Materials Required:] 600 Ironwood Beams, 300 Tempered Iron, 150 Cryo-Crystals.
[Function:] Mounts interlocking autonomous crossbow turrets along the top parapets of the perimeter wall. Fires frost-enchanted heavy bolts that freeze target mobility on impact.

’These are incredible,’ Silas thought, his gamer logic drooling over the stat boosts and defensive upgrades. ’An automated turret array and a dampening dome? If we build those, the base will be practically impregnable to standard monster hordes.’
He carefully rolled past the defensive turrets and the industrial forges, keeping his focus on their current mission. He scrolled down to the agricultural and beast-mastery section of the bundle.
He found it.
[Unlocked Blueprint:] Reinforced Beast Pavilion - Tier 2
[Type:] Specialized Military / Breeding Facility.
[Materials Required:] 600 Refined Stone, 600 Ironwood Beams, 200 Tempered Iron, 100 Deep-Earth Alloy.

[Description:] An advanced evolution of the standard wooden Beast Pen. Features reinforced ironwood stables bound with shock-absorbing Deep-Earth Alloy gates. Includes automated freshwater troughs, integrated thermal floor tiles to regulate beast body temperature during extreme weather, and an enclosed training paddock designed specifically for pack-taming and cavalry saddle-drills.
Silas turned the glowing blue scroll around, holding it out so Reina and Aeliana could see the rotating 3D wireframe diagram of the Pavilion.

"What do you think of this one?" Silas asked them. "It isn’t a basic dirt pen, but it isn’t one of those crazy over-engineered mythic breeding arenas that cost to maintain either. It sits right in the middle. Strong walls, warm floors, and an open training yard."
Aeliana leaned in with her green eyes tracing the architectural lines.

"The structural integrity is exceptional, Lord Sy. The use of Deep-Earth Alloy on the gate hinges will prevent even a Corrupted Tier 2 beast from breaking loose if it panics during the taming process. It is a very secure design."
Reina just stared at the glowing blue scroll, her heart thumping wildly against her ribs.
She was secretly in love with the design.
A standard beginner pen was just a muddy fenced-in square where beasts sat in the rain and chewed on wooden posts.
This Tier 2 Pavilion was a legitimate military installation.
The integrated thermal tiles meant her wolves wouldn’t get joint stiffness during the freezing Umbral nights.
The enclosed training paddock gave her a controlled, safe environment to run saddle drills without worrying about a spooked mount bolting into the treeline.
It was everything a Beast Tamer could ever dream of having...
She desperately wanted to tell him how perfect it was, but her lingering recruit shyness held her tongue.
She didn’t want to sound greedy or demanding.
"It... it looks very functional, My Lord," Reina said softly, trying to keep her tone professional while her eyes devoured the layout. "The paddock space is more than enough for ten mounts."
Silas didn’t miss the intense, longing sparkle in her eyes. He smiled, turning back to his interface.
"Then let’s build it," Silas declared.
He checked his synced inventory resources against the blueprint requirements:
[Refined Stone:] 2,400 / 600 (Ready)
[Ironwood Beams:] 1,800 / 600 (Ready)
[Tempered Iron:] 900 / 200 (Ready)
[Deep-Earth Alloy:] 450 / 100 (Ready)
Thanks to Thora’s relentless crushing and smelting over the last week, his armory was overflowing with refined metal.
Even the Deep-Earth Alloy requirement which would have been impossible a week ago was easily covered by the haul they had pulled from the hidden mine.
Silas took three steps back to clear the center of the tiled square.
He raised his right hand toward the designated building zone and tapped the construction prompt.
’Build!’ Silas commanded mentally.
The air in the eastern courtyard violently shifted.
The glowing blue architectural scroll in his hand shattered into a blinding storm of pixelated light.
A massive rushing wind billowed outward from the center of the square, whipping Reina’s ash-blonde braid across her face and making Aeliana’s robes flutter wildly.
An immense thirty-foot-wide three-dimensional wireframe of the Beast Pavilion projected directly onto the black stone tiles, illuminating the entire eastern wall in a brilliant azure glow.
Then, the physical matter poured in from the ether.
Heavy precision-cut blocks of refined stone slammed down from the sky, stacking upon one another with deafening sounds that shook the ground beneath their boots.
THUD! THUD! THUD!
Massive dark brown pillars of seasoned ironwood slotted seamlessly into the masonry, locking the foundation in place with loud cracks.

Molten streaks of tempered iron and dull gray Deep-Earth Alloy materialized out of thin air, wrapping around the wooden support beams, cooling instantly with loud hisses of steam to form heavy reinforced gate bars, secure drop-latches, and thick binding plates.
The entire construction took less than eight seconds.
A blinding flash of white light exploded across the courtyard, signaling the final culmination of the architecture.
When the light cleared, Reina gasped, taking a step forward.
Sitting squarely on the eastern tiles was a magnificent, brutalist military stable.
The exterior walls were built of solid, dark gray refined stone, topped with sloped ironwood roofs that would easily shed the rain.

The heavy front gates were made of thick ironwood trunks reinforced with dull gray alloy bands, leading into a spacious, impeccably paved training paddock lined with clean water troughs and individual stable stalls.
"Whoa," Reina breathed out with her eyes wide as she walked up to the fence, running her bare hand over the smooth cool metal of the alloy gate latch.
Silas didn’t stop there.
He walked up beside her, placing his palm flat against the primary stone pillar of the gate.
A familiar blue interface prompt popped up in his vision:
[Reinforced Beast Pavilion]
[Tier: 2 Construct (Rare)]
[Durability: 1,500 / 1,500]
[Status: Operational.]
[Upgrade System: Would you like to upgrade Tier 2 Reinforced Beast Pavilion to Tier 3 Mythic Pack-Lord’s Sanctuary?]
[Cost: 300 UP.]
Silas glanced at his Upgrade Point balance.
Between clearing the corrupted lab and upgrading weapons and everything, he had over a thousand UP sitting in his account waiting to be spent.
He didn’t hesitate. If he was going to build a cavalry unit, he wanted it operating at peak efficiency from day one.
’Upgrade,’ Silas commanded.
VWOOSH!
A second, even more intense wave of golden and blue energy erupted from his palm, washing over the newly built Pavilion.
The structure physically expanded.
The stone walls grew two feet thicker, shifting from standard gray stone to a dense dark obsidian masonry that matched the architecture of the main Keep.
The sloped ironwood roofs extended outward, providing deep, covered overhangs that would protect the mounts from even the worst storms.
Along the top parapets and down the center support pillars, intricate, glowing green nature runes and silver starlight symbols automatically etched themselves deep into the stone and timber.
The heavy gates shifted, the Deep-Earth Alloy bars thickening and binding with reinforced shock-absorbers.

Inside the paddock, the floor tiles glowed with a soft, warm geothermal heat, while a small automated fresh-water fountain materialized in the center of the yard, pulling clean spring water directly from the underground aquifer.
The white light faded.
[Mythic Pack-Lord’s Sanctuary]
[Tier: 3 Construct (Epic)]
[Durability: 3,500 / 3,500]
[Passive Effects:]
[Wild Tether]: Increases Beast Tamer bonding speed by 100% within the paddock.
[Primal Vigor]: Stabled beasts regenerate stamina and physical injuries at 300% standard rate.
[Nature’s Calm]: The integrated rune emits a soothing atmospheric frequency, completely eliminating beast aggression toward territorial allies and preventing panic during combat drills.
Reina stood frozen in front of the Tier 3 Sanctuary with her mouth hung open as she couldn’t even form words.
It wasn’t just a stable anymore.
It was a masterpiece of magical beast engineering.
The glowing green runes pulsing along the obsidian walls filled the air with a clean invigorating scent of pine forests and fresh rain.
Just standing near the open paddock made the Beast Tamer mana inside her own chest hum with intense ease.
She turned her head slowly, looking at Silas.
He was standing right beside her, dusting his palms off with a casual rhythm.
The afternoon sunlight caught the sharp edge of his jaw and the brilliant golden rings in his eyes.
He turned to look at her, a warm, genuine smile lighting up his entire face.
"Well?" Silas asked softly, gesturing toward the massive, rune-carved Sanctuary. "Do you like it?"
Reina felt her knees go weak. Her heart thumped so hard against her ribs it felt like it was going to break out of her chest.
She stared up at Silas.
The Lord of the Blessed Land was standing right next to her in the damp afternoon air of the Umbral Basin, waiting for her answer with a genuine casual smile on his face.

"I love it, My Lord," Reina managed to stammer out, her voice breathless and heavy with awe. "It’s perfect. The paddocks, the tiles, the Deep-Earth alloy gates... It’s exactly what my class needs to operate properly."
Silas chuckled, reaching out and clapping her gently on the shoulder.

"Glad to hear it," he said, turning his golden-ringed eyes toward the heavy ironwood gates of the new Beast Pen. "Because building the stable was only phase one. Now comes the actual hard part. We need to go out into the dark, find a pack of Corrupted Umbral Wolves, and bring them back here alive without getting our throats ripped out."
He dropped his hand from her shoulder and turned to face her fully.

"We’re going to need a hunting party to corner the pack while you establish your dominance tethers," Silas explained, slipping the Blueprints into his back pocket. "I want you to go down to the barracks and pick nine people. Anyone you want. Build your squad, and we’ll head out."
Reina blinked, completely caught off guard.

"You... you want me to pick the squad, Lord Silas?" she asked, her voice squeaking slightly as her nervous recruit instincts flared back up. "Shouldn’t you select the heavy hitters yourself? What if I pick the wrong combination of classes for a trapping mission?"
Silas shrugged his broad shoulders, looking entirely unbothered by the tactical implications.
"Anyone will do, Reina," Silas told her calmly.

He gestured casually toward the pristine silver-haired elf standing silently behind them. "As long as Aeliana is with us to lock down the area with her spells, and I’m there to handle the physical pushback, we’ll be completely fine. Go grab whoever you want to work with. We’ll meet you at the main eastern gates in twenty minutes."
He gave her a quick nod, turned around, and began walking back across the wide, black-tiled courtyard toward the Keep, with Aeliana trailing flawlessly in his shadow.

[Unlocked Blueprint:] Umbral Frost-Turret Array - Tier 2
[Type:] Automated Fortification.
[Materials Required:] 600 Ironwood Beams, 300 Tempered Iron, 150 Cryo-Crystals.
[Function:] Mounts interlocking autonomous crossbow turrets along the top parapets of the perimeter wall.
Fires frost-enchanted heavy bolts that freeze target mobility on impact.
’These are incredible,’ Silas thought, his gamer logic drooling over the stat boosts and defensive upgrades. ’An automated turret array and a dampening dome?
If we build those, the base will be practically impregnable to standard monster hordes.’
He carefully rolled past the defensive turrets and the industrial forges, keeping his focus on their current mission.
He scrolled down to the agricultural and beast-mastery section of the bundle.
He found it.
[Unlocked Blueprint:] Reinforced Beast Pavilion - Tier 2
[Type:] Specialized Military / Breeding Facility.
[Materials Required:] 600 Refined Stone, 600 Ironwood Beams, 200 Tempered Iron, 100 Deep-Earth Alloy.
[Description:] An advanced evolution of the standard wooden Beast Pen.
Features reinforced ironwood stables bound with shock-absorbing Deep-Earth Alloy gates.

Includes automated freshwater troughs, integrated thermal floor tiles to regulate beast body temperature during extreme weather, and an enclosed training paddock designed specifically for pack-taming and cavalry saddle-drills.
Silas turned the glowing blue scroll around, holding it out so Reina and Aeliana could see the rotating 3D wireframe diagram of the Pavilion.
"What do you think of this one?" Silas asked them.
"It isn’t a basic dirt pen, but it isn’t one of those crazy over-engineered mythic breeding arenas that cost to maintain either.
It sits right in the middle.
Strong walls, warm floors, and an open training yard."
Aeliana leaned in with her green eyes tracing the architectural lines.
"The structural integrity is exceptional, Lord Sy.
The use of Deep-Earth Alloy on the gate hinges will prevent even a Corrupted Tier 2 beast from breaking loose if it panics during the taming process.
It is a very secure design."
Reina just stared at the glowing blue scroll, her heart thumping wildly against her ribs.
She was secretly in love with the design.
A standard beginner pen was just a muddy fenced-in square where beasts sat in the rain and chewed on wooden posts.
This Tier 2 Pavilion was a legitimate military installation.
The integrated thermal tiles meant her wolves wouldn’t get joint stiffness during the freezing Umbral nights.
The enclosed training paddock gave her a controlled, safe environment to run saddle drills without worrying about a spooked mount bolting into the treeline.
It was everything a Beast Tamer could ever dream of having...
She desperately wanted to tell him how perfect it was, but her lingering recruit shyness held her tongue.
She didn’t want to sound greedy or demanding.
"It... it looks very functional, My Lord," Reina said softly, trying to keep her tone professional while her eyes devoured the layout.
"The paddock space is more than enough for ten mounts."
Silas didn’t miss the intense, longing sparkle in her eyes.
He smiled, turning back to his interface.
"Then let’s build it," Silas declared.
He checked his synced inventory resources against the blueprint requirements:
[Refined Stone:] 2,400 / 600 (Ready)
[Ironwood Beams:] 1,800 / 600 (Ready)
[Tempered Iron:] 900 / 200 (Ready)
[Deep-Earth Alloy:] 450 / 100 (Ready)
Thanks to Thora’s relentless crushing and smelting over the last week, his armory was overflowing with refined metal.
Even the Deep-Earth Alloy requirement which would have been impossible a week ago was easily covered by the haul they had pulled from the hidden mine.
Silas took three steps back to clear the center of the tiled square.
He raised his right hand toward the designated building zone and tapped the construction prompt.
’Build!’ Silas commanded mentally.
The air in the eastern courtyard violently shifted.
The glowing blue architectural scroll in his hand shattered into a blinding storm of pixelated light.
A massive rushing wind billowed outward from the center of the square, whipping Reina’s ash-blonde braid across her face and making Aeliana’s robes flutter wildly.
An immense thirty-foot-wide three-dimensional wireframe of the Beast Pavilion projected directly onto the black stone tiles, illuminating the entire eastern wall in a brilliant azure glow.
Then, the physical matter poured in from the ether.
Heavy precision-cut blocks of refined stone slammed down from the sky, stacking upon one another with deafening sounds that shook the ground beneath their boots.
THUD!
THUD!
THUD!
Massive dark brown pillars of seasoned ironwood slotted seamlessly into the masonry, locking the foundation in place with loud cracks.

Molten streaks of tempered iron and dull gray Deep-Earth Alloy materialized out of thin air, wrapping around the wooden support beams, cooling instantly with loud hisses of steam to form heavy reinforced gate bars, secure drop-latches, and thick binding plates.
The entire construction took less than eight seconds.
A blinding flash of white light exploded across the courtyard, signaling the final culmination of the architecture.
When the light cleared, Reina gasped, taking a step forward.
Sitting squarely on the eastern tiles was a magnificent, brutalist military stable.
The exterior walls were built of solid, dark gray refined stone, topped with sloped ironwood roofs that would easily shed the rain.

The heavy front gates were made of thick ironwood trunks reinforced with dull gray alloy bands, leading into a spacious, impeccably paved training paddock lined with clean water troughs and individual stable stalls.
"Whoa," Reina breathed out with her eyes wide as she walked up to the fence, running her bare hand over the smooth cool metal of the alloy gate latch.
Silas didn’t stop there.
He walked up beside her, placing his palm flat against the primary stone pillar of the gate.
A familiar blue interface prompt popped up in his vision:
[Reinforced Beast Pavilion]
[Tier: 2 Construct (Rare)]
[Durability: 1,500 / 1,500]
[Status: Operational.]
[Upgrade System: Would you like to upgrade Tier 2 Reinforced Beast Pavilion to Tier 3 Mythic Pack-Lord’s Sanctuary?]
[Cost: 300 UP.]
Silas glanced at his Upgrade Point balance.
Between clearing the corrupted lab and upgrading weapons and everything, he had over a thousand UP sitting in his account waiting to be spent.
He didn’t hesitate.
If he was going to build a cavalry unit, he wanted it operating at peak efficiency from day one.
’Upgrade,’ Silas commanded.
VWOOSH!
A second, even more intense wave of golden and blue energy erupted from his palm, washing over the newly built Pavilion.
The structure physically expanded.
The stone walls grew two feet thicker, shifting from standard gray stone to a dense dark obsidian masonry that matched the architecture of the main Keep.
The sloped ironwood roofs extended outward, providing deep, covered overhangs that would protect the mounts from even the worst storms.
Along the top parapets and down the center support pillars, intricate, glowing green nature runes and silver starlight symbols automatically etched themselves deep into the stone and timber.
The heavy gates shifted, the Deep-Earth Alloy bars thickening and binding with reinforced shock-absorbers.

Inside the paddock, the floor tiles glowed with a soft, warm geothermal heat, while a small automated fresh-water fountain materialized in the center of the yard, pulling clean spring water directly from the underground aquifer.
The white light faded.
[Mythic Pack-Lord’s Sanctuary]
[Tier: 3 Construct (Epic)]
[Durability: 3,500 / 3,500]
[Passive Effects:]
[Wild Tether]: Increases Beast Tamer bonding speed by 100% within the paddock.
[Primal Vigor]: Stabled beasts regenerate stamina and physical injuries at 300% standard rate.
[Nature’s Calm]: The integrated rune emits a soothing atmospheric frequency, completely eliminating beast aggression toward territorial allies and preventing panic during combat drills.
Reina stood frozen in front of the Tier 3 Sanctuary with her mouth hung open as she couldn’t even form words.
It wasn’t just a stable anymore.
It was a masterpiece of magical beast engineering.
The glowing green runes pulsing along the obsidian walls filled the air with a clean invigorating scent of pine forests and fresh rain.
Just standing near the open paddock made the Beast Tamer mana inside her own chest hum with intense ease.
She turned her head slowly, looking at Silas.
He was standing right beside her, dusting his palms off with a casual rhythm.
The afternoon sunlight caught the sharp edge of his jaw and the brilliant golden rings in his eyes.
He turned to look at her, a warm, genuine smile lighting up his entire face.
"Well?" Silas asked softly, gesturing toward the massive, rune-carved Sanctuary.
"Do you like it?"
Reina felt her knees go weak.
Her heart thumped so hard against her ribs it felt like it was going to break out of her chest.
She stared up at Silas.
The Lord of the Blessed Land was standing right next to her in the damp afternoon air of the Umbral Basin, waiting for her answer with a genuine casual smile on his face.
"I love it, My Lord," Reina managed to stammer out, her voice breathless and heavy with awe.
"It’s perfect.
The paddocks, the tiles, the Deep-Earth alloy gates...
It’s exactly what my class needs to operate properly."
Silas chuckled, reaching out and clapping her gently on the shoulder.
"Glad to hear it," he said, turning his golden-ringed eyes toward the heavy ironwood gates of the new Beast Pen.
"Because building the stable was only phase one.
Now comes the actual hard part.
We need to go out into the dark, find a pack of Corrupted Umbral Wolves, and bring them back here alive without getting our throats ripped out."
He dropped his hand from her shoulder and turned to face her fully.
"We’re going to need a hunting party to corner the pack while you establish your dominance tethers," Silas explained, slipping the Blueprints into his back pocket.
"I want you to go down to the barracks and pick nine people.
Anyone you want.
Build your squad, and we’ll head out."
Reina blinked, completely caught off guard.
"You... you want me to pick the squad, Lord Silas?" she asked, her voice squeaking slightly as her nervous recruit instincts flared back up.
"Shouldn’t you select the heavy hitters yourself?
What if I pick the wrong combination of classes for a trapping mission?"
Silas shrugged his broad shoulders, looking entirely unbothered by the tactical implications.
"Anyone will do, Reina," Silas told her calmly.
He gestured casually toward the pristine silver-haired elf standing silently behind them.
"As long as Aeliana is with us to lock down the area with her spells, and I’m there to handle the physical pushback, we’ll be completely fine.
Go grab whoever you want to work with.
We’ll meet you at the main eastern gates in twenty minutes."
He gave her a quick nod, turned around, and began walking back across the wide, black-tiled courtyard toward the Keep, with Aeliana trailing flawlessly in his shadow.

chapters.title: Chapter 121: Choosing A Team
paragraphs: Reina stood alone in front of the Beast Pen for a few seconds, processing the weight of the authority he had just handed her.
He was letting a mid-tier recruit build the actual raid squad for their first major cavalry mission.

’He said anyone will do...’ Reina thought, her mind rapidly calculating the survival odds of walking into the dangerous Unknown Zone outside their walls. ’He thinks we’re safe just because he and Aeliana are there but I’m not taking any chances. If we’re going out to wrestle Corrupted Wolves in the mud, I am not bringing a bunch of soft archers who don’t know how to take a hit.’
She spun on her heel and broke into a dead sprint toward the Warlord Garrison.
She wasn’t going to pull random names from a hat. She was going straight to the top of the food chain as she was going to recruit the commanders.
Reina charged through the heavy double doors of the barracks, her boots tracking mud onto the polished stone floor.
The main hall of the garrison was loud and chaotic, filled with dozens of off-duty infantry girls cleaning their weapons, eating spiced jerky, or playing cards at the long wooden tables.
She ignored all of them and headed straight for the quarters located in the north wing.
She stopped in front of a heavy wooden door that was cracked slightly open.
Inside the room, sitting on the edge of an oversized reinforced ironwood cot, was Captain Brida.
The brawler wasn’t wearing her usual heavy plate armor.
She was dressed down in a simple, sleeveless gray canvas shirt and loose training pants, her thick muscled arms were completely bare.
Brida wasn’t resting.

She was aggressively rolling her broad shoulders, throwing sharp high-speed shadow punches into the empty air. Her face was flushed a deep bright pink, and a goofy uncharacteristic smile was plastered across her rugged face as she stared blankly at the wall.

"Take that, you giant squid..." Brida muttered to herself, throwing a fierce left hook before giggling softly. "Yeah, block that with your tentacles... Oh wait, my Lord is watching. I have to look fierce. Roar!"
Reina stopped dead in her tracks with her hand hovering over the doorframe.

’What in the name of the world is she doing?’ Reina thought, her jaw dropping slightly as she watched the six-foot battle-hardened commander giggle and blush like a teenage girl while punching the air.
Reina cleared her throat loudly and knocked her knuckles against the heavy wood of the doorframe.
Brida violently flinched.
The woman snapped out of her lovestruck daydream in a fraction of a second, her combat instincts taking over.
She dropped into a heavy brawler’s stance with her thick fists raised as her eyes locked onto the doorway with pure aggression.
When she saw Reina standing there, the aggression vanished, replaced instantly by a deep defensive embarrassment.

"What?!" Brida barked loudly, her face flushing even redder as she quickly sat back down on the edge of her cot and crossed her arms over her chest. "I wasn’t doing anything! I was just practicing my footwork! What do you want, recruit?"
Reina decided to pretend she hadn’t seen a single thing.

"Captain Brida," Reina said respectfully, keeping her posture straight. "Lord Silas just finished building the new Beast Pavilion in the eastern courtyard. We’re heading out the main gates in fifteen minutes to hunt and trap a pack of Corrupted Umbral Wolves. He put me in charge of assembling the hunting party. I need a heavy frontline brawler who can take a hit and hold a wolf down without killing it."
Brida’s embarrassment evaporated instantly. Her eyes lit up with fierce excitement at the prospect of a real fight.

"A wolf hunt?" Brida grinned, cracking her thick knuckles with a loud meaty pop. "Now you’re speaking my language, Tamer. Poking wooden dummies in the mud all morning was putting me to sleep. I’m in..."
She stood up from the cot, grabbing her heavy leather chestplate from the weapon rack.
Before she strapped it on, she stopped, looking down at the sleeveless gray canvas shirt she was wearing.
She looked back up at Reina, her fierce expression softening into unexpected vulnerability.

"Hey, kid," Brida asked quietly, gesturing awkwardly to her own heavily muscled chest and arms. "Does this shirt look okay? The Captain is going to be out there, and I don’t want to look like a complete slob next to Aeliana. Does it show off my biceps enough?"
Reina blinked, completely thrown off balance by the question.
The idea that a towering warrior woman cared about her bicep definition purely to impress the Warlord was both terrifying and deeply relatable.
"It looks incredibly strong, Captain," Reina nodded quickly, offering a reassuring smile. "Your arms look huge."
"Perfect," Brida beamed, slapping her heavy pauldron into place. "Go gather the rest of your squad. I’ll meet you at the gate."
Reina turned and jogged back down the corridor with her mind struggling to process the interaction.
’This whole territory is completely gone for him,’ Reina thought, shaking her head. ’Even the heavy brawlers are blushing. It’s ridiculous...’
She liked him but not to that level, was he casting some sort of spell?
Her next stop was the communal washroom located behind the mess hall.
If she needed precision and lockdown tactics to trap a wolf without killing it, she needed the territory’s best Huntress.
She pushed the swinging wooden doors open and stepped into the humid, soapy air of the laundry room.
Tasmin was standing in front of a long row of deep wooden basins with her sleeves rolled up, scrubbing a pile of clothes against a ridged washboard.
The Huntress was serving a heavy punishment.
That punishment for nearly getting herself killed by the orc had finally caught up to Tasmin.
Silas had chewed her out in front of all of the girls and assigned her to manual laundry duty for an entire month to teach her the value of following orders.
Currently, Tasmin was scowling down at a massive sudsy wooden bowl filled entirely with the dirty undergarments of the infantry girls.
The Huntress held up a pair of massive heavy-duty canvas bloomers that clearly belonged to Brida.
The thick fabric was soaked with dirty soapy water and Tasmin’s nose wrinkled in disgust as she dropped them back into the bowl.

"Disgusting," Tasmin muttered under her breath, wiping a strand of wet dark hair out of her eyes with her forearm. "I kill beasts and I cut throats in the dark. I shouldn’t be washing the sweat out of Brida’s underwear."
"Commander Tasmin?" Reina called out softly, stepping into the room.
Tasmin stiffened, quickly dropping her hands back into the soapy water and schooling her face into a blank professional mask.
She looked over her shoulder at the recruit.
"Reina," Tasmin acknowledged smoothly, her dark eyes sharp despite her humiliating current assignment. "What do you need? Did you tear your tunic during the spear drills again?"

"No, Commander," Reina shook her head, walking closer to the basins. "Lord Silas is taking me outside the walls to hunt Umbral Wolves for the new Beast Pavilion. He gave me the authority to pick the squad. You taught me how to operate in the wild during my first week here. I need someone who can set high-tensile snares in the dark without alerting the pack so in short, I need you on the squad."
Tasmin paused, her hands still submerged in the soapy water.
For a second, a flash of genuine interest sparked in the Huntress’s eyes.
The chance to drop the miserable laundry assignment, grab her chained Short swords, and step back out into the Unknown Zone alongside her Lord was an incredibly tempting offer.
But then, Tasmin looked down at the massive bowl of dirty canvas bloomers. She sighed with her shoulders slumping slightly.
"I have to decline the offer, Reina," Tasmin said quietly, pulling her hands out of the water and drying them on a towel.
Reina frowned in confusion. "Why? You hate laundry duty. Lord Silas wouldn’t mind if you took a break for an official military operation."

"That’s exactly why I can’t go," Tasmin corrected her, her voice turning strict and deeply respectful. "You are my student, Reina. I taught you how to move quietly in the brush. I want to see you succeed out there but the Lord gave me a direct order to finish this assignment. If I abandon this post just because a fun hunting trip came up, I prove that I haven’t learned my lesson about discipline."
She picked up her scrubbing brush, turning back to the miserable pile of wet clothes with renewed stubborn determination.

"Go out there and catch your wolves, Tamer," Tasmin told her over her shoulder. "Show the Lord that my tracking lessons didn’t go to waste. I’ll stay here and finish my punishment... I owe him that much."
Reina stood there for a second, surprised.

’She’s passing up a chance to go on a mission with him?’ Reina thought, her assumptions taking another heavy hit. ’She actually respects his authority enough to scrub dirty underwear instead of taking the easy way out. He really commands her loyalty...’
"Thank you, Commander," Reina said softly, giving the assassin a deep, respectful bow before turning and leaving the washroom.
She checked the time.
She only had ten minutes left before she had to be at the gates so she needed more bodies.
Reina jogged out into the main training yard, looking for the head scout.
Fenna was sitting on a wooden bench near the archery targets, carefully re-stringing her longbow with a fresh piece of treated spider-silk.
The tall sharp-eyed scout looked up as Reina approached, offering a friendly nod.
"Hey, Reina," Fenna greeted her. "Heard you got pulled up to the big office. Did the Boss actually read your pitch?"

"He did," Reina confirmed, catching her breath. "We built the Beast Pen. We’re heading out to trap the wolves right now. I’m building the squad, and I need a long-range spotter to sit in the trees and track the pack’s movements. I want you to come with us."
Fenna smiled, pulling the tension tight on her bowstring.
It was a great offer. Any girl in the barracks would jump at the chance to leave the mud behind and go on an elite raid with the Lord but Fenna shook her head.
"I appreciate the invite, Reina," Fenna said genuinely, resting her bow across her knees. "But I’m going to pass."
Reina blinked, completely caught off guard for the second time in ten minutes. "You don’t want to go? It’s a direct operation with Lord Silas."

"Of course I want to go," Fenna laughed, pointing a thumb toward the distant Keep. "The man is gorgeous, he’s amazing... too amazing really and he fights like a demon but I’ve been on the many raids with him. I’ve had my time in the spotlight so you should take Elara instead."
Fenna gestured across the yard toward the junior scout, who was currently practicing her draw speed against a straw target.

"Elara is young, but her eyesight is sharper than mine in the dark," Fenna explained with her voice lacking jealousy or ego. "She needs the field experience, and she deserves a chance to show the Boss what she can do. Give the junior girls a shot, Reina. The Lord likes it when we lift each other up."
Reina just stood there, staring at the older scout in total silence.
Her internal perspective of the women at the top was entirely shattering.
When she first arrived at the Blessed Land, she assumed the elite girls were a toxic competitive crew who fought tooth and nail for every second of the Lord’s attention.
She assumed they hoarded the glory and looked down on the regular recruits but that wasn’t true at all.
Tasmin was scrubbing laundry out of pure respect for his orders.
Fenna was actively stepping aside to let a junior scout get some face time with the commander.
They were a real, functioning military brotherhood that actually cared about developing the lower ranks.
’They really believe in what he’s building here?’ Reina realized with a warm unexpected feeling of genuine camaraderie blooming in her chest. ’And they want me to succeed.’
"You’re right, Fenna," Reina smiled warmly, nodding her head. "I’ll go grab Elara. Thank you."
With her perspective completely shifted, Reina didn’t bother trying to recruit the rest of the elite.
She realized Silas hadn’t told her to pick ’anyone’ because he didn’t care... he told her to pick anyone because he wanted her to rely on her own peers.

Fenna was sitting on a wooden bench near the archery targets, carefully re-stringing her longbow with a fresh piece of treated spider-silk.
The tall sharp-eyed scout looked up as Reina approached, offering a friendly nod.
"Hey, Reina," Fenna greeted her.
"Heard you got pulled up to the big office.
Did the Boss actually read your pitch?"
"He did," Reina confirmed, catching her breath.
"We built the Beast Pen.
We’re heading out to trap the wolves right now.
I’m building the squad, and I need a long-range spotter to sit in the trees and track the pack’s movements.
I want you to come with us."
Fenna smiled, pulling the tension tight on her bowstring.
It was a great offer.
Any girl in the barracks would jump at the chance to leave the mud behind and go on an elite raid with the Lord but Fenna shook her head.
"I appreciate the invite, Reina," Fenna said genuinely, resting her bow across her knees.
"But I’m going to pass."
Reina blinked, completely caught off guard for the second time in ten minutes.
"You don’t want to go?
It’s a direct operation with Lord Silas."
"Of course I want to go," Fenna laughed, pointing a thumb toward the distant Keep.
"The man is gorgeous, he’s amazing... too amazing really and he fights like a demon but I’ve been on the many raids with him.
I’ve had my time in the spotlight so you should take Elara instead."
Fenna gestured across the yard toward the junior scout, who was currently practicing her draw speed against a straw target.
"Elara is young, but her eyesight is sharper than mine in the dark," Fenna explained with her voice lacking jealousy or ego.
"She needs the field experience, and she deserves a chance to show the Boss what she can do.
Give the junior girls a shot, Reina.
The Lord likes it when we lift each other up."
Reina just stood there, staring at the older scout in total silence.
Her internal perspective of the women at the top was entirely shattering.
When she first arrived at the Blessed Land, she assumed the elite girls were a toxic competitive crew who fought tooth and nail for every second of the Lord’s attention.
She assumed they hoarded the glory and looked down on the regular recruits but that wasn’t true at all.
Tasmin was scrubbing laundry out of pure respect for his orders.
Fenna was actively stepping aside to let a junior scout get some face time with the commander.
They were a real, functioning military brotherhood that actually cared about developing the lower ranks.
’They really believe in what he’s building here?’ Reina realized with a warm unexpected feeling of genuine camaraderie blooming in her chest. ’And they want me to succeed.’
"You’re right, Fenna," Reina smiled warmly, nodding her head.
"I’ll go grab Elara.
Thank you."
With her perspective completely shifted, Reina didn’t bother trying to recruit the rest of the elite.
She realized Silas hadn’t told her to pick ’anyone’ because he didn’t care... he told her to pick anyone because he wanted her to rely on her own peers.

chapters.title: Chapter 122: Outside The Walls
paragraphs: She ran across the training yard, waving her hands to get the attention of her own friends... the mid-tier girls she had been suffering in the mud with all week.
"Elara! Vala! Kaal!" Reina shouted, calling out eight names from the infantry and scout blocks. "Drop the training gear! Grab your field kits and heavy ropes! We’re going on a raid with the Lord!"
The girls dropped their wooden spears and practice bows, their faces lighting up with pure shock and excitement.
They scrambled toward the armory to grab their real weapons, chattering frantically about getting to see Silas fight up close.
Fifteen minutes later, Reina and her newly assembled squad of girls jogged across the eastern tiles and approached the towering black steel-weave gates of the Blessed Land.
Silas was already standing there waiting for them.
The Lord wasn’t wearing his casual black shirt anymore. He was fully geared up for the Unknown Zone.
He wore his heavy, dark steel-weave chestplate, his thick leather boots, and his dark canvas trousers.
The heavy, silver-patterned hand-and-a-half blade he had forged that morning hung securely at his hip, radiating a dangerous aura of starlight.
Standing right beside him, looking completely pristine and untouched by the grime of the world, was Aeliana and clinging tightly to his right arm, practically vibrating with joy, was Brida.
The commander had her heavy Kraken shield strapped to her forearm, and she was leaning her shoulder against his bicep with a wide grin on her face.
Silas looked up as Reina and the eight junior girls approached.
He let out a long quiet sigh, gently trying to pry his arm loose from Brida’s iron grip without much success.

"Welcome to the hunting party, ladies," Silas greeted them with his deep voice calm and commanding as he looked over the excited nervous faces of the regular infantry girls. "I apologize for interrupting your afternoon drills, but we have a major logistical upgrade to execute, and I need your muscle."
He gestured toward Reina, who was standing at the front of the pack with her snare ropes coiled over her shoulder.

"This entire operation is happening because Reina noticed a flaw in our patrol stamina and pitched a solution," Silas announced to the squad, making sure every single girl heard him clearly. "She designed the Beast Pavilion, and she’s going to lead the taming process today. Follow her calls when we find the pack."
The eight infantry girls immediately turned to Reina as their went eyes wide with respect.
"You designed that massive place?" Elara whispered in awe.
"That was your idea?" Vala gasped, clapping Reina on the back. "That’s incredible, Reina! You’re going to get us off foot patrol!"
Reina’s face flushed bright red again, but this time, it wasn’t from embarrassment.
It was from pure pride.

Silas hadn’t taken credit for the build even though he had been the one to build it... He had publicly handed the glory directly to her in front of her peers, elevating her status in the barracks instantly.
She stood up straighter, gripping her snare ropes tight.
"Alright," Silas said, drawing his hand-and-a-half blade from its sheath.

The dark steel hummed softly in the damp air. "The Unknown Zone is hostile territory. Keep your eyes on the treeline. Do not break formation, and do not engage a monster until Reina gives the signal to drop the snares. If a Corrupted Alpha breaks the line, fall back and let me or Brida handle the impact."
He turned toward the two heavy-infantry girls stationed at the gate cranks.
"Raise the gates!" Silas ordered.
The two girls grabbed the massive iron wheels and threw their backs into it.
With a loud grinding screech, the heavy steel-weave portcullis slowly dragged upward, revealing the dark terrifying ironwood forest of the Umbral Basin lying just beyond their safe stone tiles.
The cold wind of the Unknown Zone blew into the courtyard, smelling like wet decay.
"Move out," Silas commanded, stepping past the threshold and into the mud of the wild.
Brida marched right beside him, her battleaxe resting on her shoulder. Aeliana floated silently behind them with her hands glowing as she primed her defensive spells.
Reina took a deep breath, stepping through the gates alongside Elara and the rest of the junior squad. She looked at the broad armored back of the Warlord leading them into the dark.
He had listened to her, He had praised her in front of her friends, and now he was walking into danger just to help her fulfill her class potential.

’I won’t disappoint you, My Lord,’ Reina thought fiercely with her heart completely surrendered to the cause as she marched into the forest. ’I’m going to build you the greatest cavalry unit this world has ever seen.’

The heavy, iron-reinforced gates of the Blessed Land slowly ground shut behind them, the massive steel-weave portcullis dropping into the mud with a resounding crash that echoed through the damp trees.
The exact second that gate hit the dirt, the entire atmosphere shifted.
Inside the walls, the territory smelled like roasting meat, woodsmoke, and the clean scent of Thora’s forge.
Out here in the Unknown Zone, the Umbral Basin smelled like wet rot, swamp water, and suffocating decay.
The massive towering ironwood trees blocked out the bruised purple sunlight, casting long, jagged shadows across the forest floor.
Silas stood at the front of the formation, his boots sinking a half-inch into the soft, treacherous black mud.
He rested his right hand casually on the pommel of his newly forged hand-and-a-half sword, feeling the comforting hum of the starlight Damascus steel vibrating against his palm.
He didn’t draw the weapon. He simply turned to his right and looked down at the ash-blonde Beast Tamer standing beside him.
"Alright, Reina," Silas said, his deep voice carrying clearly over the rustling leaves and the distant sounds of the swamp. "Your show."
Reina blinked, her hands tightening around the heavy coils of thick, treated trapping rope slung over her shoulder.
She looked up at him, a flicker of nervous hesitation crossing her face. "My Lord?"

"I don’t know the first thing about tracking a wild animal, let alone a corrupted monster..." Silas explained, stepping back to formally surrender the point position to her. "I’m a Lord. My job is managing logistics and hitting things very hard when they try to bite us. You are the Beast Tamer. I want to see exactly how you plan to push a pack of apex predators under your control. You lead the way and we follow your calls."
Reina’s chest swelled.
The anxiety that had plagued her all week completely evaporated, replaced by a surge of fierce pride and a bit of shyness..
He wasn’t just bringing her along as a token guide so he could do the heavy lifting himself; he was legitimately placing the success of the entire operation squarely on her shoulders.
"Understood, Lord Silas," Reina said with her voice dropping its nervous edge and taking on a sharp tone.
She offered him a quick respectful nod. "Thank you. I won’t let anyone down."
She turned around to face the squad of eight junior infantry girls, the towering Brida, and the silently floating Arcanist, Aeliana.

"Keep your footsteps light!" Reina ordered the squad with her eyes scanning the dark dense underbrush of the ironwood forest. "Umbral Wolves have hyper-sensitive hearing. If you snap a dead branch, they will hear us coming from a mile away... Do not draw your weapons unless I give the signal. The scrape of steel leaving a scabbard sounds like a dinner bell to a starving pack."
The junior girls nodded quickly, adjusting their leather belts and making sure their gear was tied down tight so it wouldn’t rattle.

Reina turned back to the treeline and dropped into a low crouch. She didn’t look at the horizon though, instead she looked straight down at the wet, black mud near the roots of a massive rotting tree stump.
She reached out with her bare fingers, gently brushing aside a cluster of damp, heavy ferns.
"Here," Reina whispered, pointing to a series of deep, massive indentations pressed into the muck.
The junior girls crowded around, peering over her shoulder.
The footprints were massive... easily the size of a standard dinner plate with four distinct toe pads and deep gouges dug into the earth right at the front of the print.

"Wolf-type monsters usually leave these exact kinds of tracks," Reina educated the squad, tracing the edge of the print with her index finger without actually touching the mud. "Notice how the claw marks are dug deep into the front of the track, while the back heel pad is barely pressed into the dirt? Standard wolves distribute their weight evenly when they’re walking or patrolling."
She stood up, pointing her finger deeper into the dark, tangled brush.

"But these claws didn’t retract, and the weight is thrown entirely forward," Reina continued with her Beast Tamer instincts actively processing the environmental data. "That means they were digging in for traction. They weren’t just wandering through here... They were actively running. Something spooked them, or they were chasing prey. The mud hasn’t filled back into the claw gouges yet, and the water pooling at the bottom is still cloudy. These tracks are fresh so probably less than an hour old."
Silas watched her work with genuine appreciation.

’That is exactly why you recruit specialized classes,’ He thought. ’If I was out here alone, I would have just walked right past that mud puddle and wandered aimlessly into the swamp until something tried to eat my face... She’s reading the dirt like a book, like Tasmin.’
"Follow the trail," Reina commanded, slipping seamlessly into the role of squad leader. "Keep your eyes on the brush. They moved east."
The hunting party fell into a loose formation. Reina took point, tracking the disturbed mud and broken twigs.
Silas walked a few paces behind her, acting as the primary physical shield, while Brida guarded his flank.
Aeliana drifted quietly at the rear, her glowing silver eyes scanning the high canopy for aerial threats, while the eight junior girls filled the middle of the pack.
As they pushed deeper into the Unknown Zone, the initial terrifying tension of leaving the safe walls began to slowly fade.
The forest was dark and creepy, but with Silas and two important women casually walking alongside them, the junior infantry girls started to relax.
And when a group of bored, isolated military recruits started to relax, the conversation inevitably drifted toward the one topic they all obsessively gossiped about in the barracks...
"Lord Silas," Vala, a short energetic shieldmaiden, whispered from the middle of the pack, trying to keep her voice down so she wouldn’t spook the woods. "Can I ask you a question about your gear?"
Silas didn’t turn around, keeping his eyes on the dark trees ahead. "Go ahead, Vala."

"That sword you forged last week," Vala asked, staring at the dark gray, silver-patterned hilt resting on his hip. "The commanders were talking about it in the mess hall. They said you folded virgin silver directly into the core and it created a magic circle that makes the blade unbreakable... Is that true? Or is Thora just exaggerating again?"

"It’s true," Silas answered casually, stepping over a thick rotting root. "The silver reacts to high-density mana. It creates a reinforcement loop so basically, the harder I swing it, the harder the metal gets."
A soft chorus of impressed murmurs rippled through the junior girls.

"That’s so unfair," Kaal, a lean spear-fighter, whispered with a grin. "You already have one of the highest physical strength stats in the entire territory, and now you have a sword that can’t break. Do you ever actually get tired during a raid, My Lord? Or do you just have an endless cheat code for stamina?"
Silas chuckled, ducking under a low-hanging branch.
"I get tired. The Core regenerates my energy reserves faster than a standard human, but if I swing a heavy piece of iron for six hours straight, my shoulders burn just like anyone else’s."
The conversation started innocent enough, but the girls were recruits.
They spent all day practicing spear thrusts in the mud and talking in the dark.
Once they realized Silas wasn’t going to punish them for speaking out of turn, the questions rapidly escalated.
"Is it true you fought a Kraken bare-handed?" Elara asked with her eyes wide.
"Eh? I didn’t fight a Kraken but a Mire-Drake." Silas corrected her.

chapters.title: Chapter 123: A Battle To The Death
paragraphs: "What about the rumors from the upper Keep?" another girl chimed in, her tone turning slightly mischievous. "The girls on laundry duty said they wash your shirts, and they’re always completely shredded... Do you really go through three shirts a week just from flexing too hard?"
"That’s mostly from monsters trying to claw my chest open," Silas deadpanned, fighting a sigh. "Not flexing."
"Speaking of the Keep..." Kaal leaned forward, a devious inappropriate smirk spreading across her face.
She lowered her voice to a conspiratorial whisper.

"We all know the commanders have their own private washrooms up there but the rumor in the barracks is that the Lord doesn’t bathe alone. Is it true you share the tub with the Goddess and the Pirate Queen?"
The entire squad of junior girls gasped, a collective scandalous giggle erupting from the middle of the formation.
A few of them blushed furiously, turning their heads away, while the bolder ones stared directly at Silas’s broad back, desperately waiting for him to answer the perverted question.
Silas closed his eyes for a fraction of a second, feeling a massive, throbbing headache forming right behind his temples.

’I am trying to run a professional military operation...’ Silas thought, groaning internally. ’And my troops are acting like a bunch of high schoolers at a sleepover. This base has zero HR oversight.’
Before Silas could formulate a proper socially acceptable response that would shut the rumors down without causing a riot, a muscular arm violently wrapped around his bicep.
Brida stepped aggressively into the center of the formation.

The towering commander didn’t just hook his arm... she yanked Silas firmly against her side, pressing the heavy, dense muscle of her shoulder and the soft swell of her massive chest directly against his ribcage.
She glared over her shoulder at the squad of giggling recruits as her stormy eyes flashed with fierce possessiveness.

"Alright, back off, you nosy little grunts..." Brida barked, her booming voice completely devoid of any real anger, but dripping with smug superiority. "The Boss’s bathing habits are strictly classified command business and even if he did share a tub, you lot aren’t high enough level to earn a spot in the water."
She squeezed Silas’s arm tighter, leaning her head against his shoulder and offering the junior girls a wicked, highly arrogant grin.

"Besides," Brida boasted, puffing her chest out. "The Captain is busy today. He’s my personal escort for this raid... He’s mine for the afternoon, so keep your perverted questions to yourselves and keep your eyes on the trees before a swamp-troll eats you."
The junior girls immediately erupted into a chorus of disappointed groans and jealous complaints.
"That’s so unfair, Commander!" Vala whined, pouting. "You get to hang out with him all the time during raids!"
"Yeah, stop hogging the Lord!" Kaal grumbled, crossing her arms. "We want a turn to hold his arm!"
"Rank has its privileges, ladies!" Brida laughed loudly, completely ignoring their complaints and refusing to let go of Silas’s bicep.
Silas just sighed, shaking his head.
He didn’t pull away from the woman.

If letting Brida cling to his arm kept the recruits from asking any more highly invasive questions about his private life, he was perfectly fine being used as a piece of armed arm-candy for the afternoon.
"Quiet."
Reina’s voice cut through the banter like a whip.
The playful joking atmosphere in the squad vanished in a single microsecond.
Reina had stopped dead in her tracks about twenty yards ahead of them.
She wasn’t crouching to look at mud tracks anymore. She was standing perfectly upright with her body rigid as her hand was resting firmly on the hilt of the hunting knife strapped to her thigh.
Silas immediately dropped the casual demeanor.
He gently untangled his arm from Brida’s grip, stepping forward with his hand dropping back to his sword hilt.
"What do you see, Reina?" Silas asked quietly, his eyes scanning the dark oppressive treeline.
Reina motioned for him to come closer.
Silas stepped up to the Beast Tamer. Reina pointed to the thick moss-covered trunk of a massive ironwood tree directly to their left.
Splattered across the dark green moss, roughly four feet off the ground, was a massive, fresh streak of thick dark crimson blood.

"The tracks changed," Reina whispered tightly. "The claw marks aren’t uniform anymore... They’re chaotic. Deep gouges tearing the roots up, overlapping footprints and scuff marks indicating something heavy was dragging its back legs."
She looked up at Silas, her face pale but determined.

"They didn’t just run through here. They were ambushed. We’re tracking a pack that is actively bleeding, and we might be walking straight into whatever hurt them. Keep your guard up as we are getting very close to a fight."
Silas nodded with a sigh.
He looked back at the squad. "Weapons drawn and no more talking. We must move silently."
The junior girls drew their shortswords and nocked arrows to their bowstrings, the metallic scrape of steel barely making a sound as they prepared for combat.
As they slowly crept forward, following the bloody trail through the dense ferns, Reina fell back a half-step to walk directly beside Silas.

"Lord Silas," Reina whispered, keeping her eyes scanning the dark brush. "If we find the pack, and they are in a compromised state, we need to execute the trapping plan flawlessly... We cannot just grab random wolves and drag them back to the Sanctuary. If we want to breed a functional high-endurance cavalry unit, we need specific pack dynamics."
"Tell me what you need," Silas replied, his eyes locked forward.

"I need several healthy females to establish the breeding core," Reina explained clinically. "If there are any cubs or juveniles, we prioritize capturing them... Cubs are incredibly malleable; if I bond with them while they’re young, they will view the Garrison as their natural den, completely eliminating the need to break wild aggression."
She paused, taking a breath.

"But most importantly, I need at least one, preferably two, strong Alpha males. A wolf pack’s social hierarchy is built entirely around the dominant male. If I can mentally break an Alpha male and tether him to my command, the females and the cubs will automatically submit to the territory... Without a male, the pack structure will collapse, and they will fight the saddles to the death."
Silas nodded, absorbing the tactical information. "Understood. Females, cubs, and an Alpha male."
He took two more steps through the mud before his Warlord brain violently hit the brakes.
Silas froze mid-stride, his boot sinking into the muck. His heart skipped a beat, a sudden, terrifying realization slamming into his mind like a physical blow.
’Wait a damn minute,’ Silas panicked internally, his eyes widening as he stared at the dark trees. ’A male?’
He remembered sitting in the dirt of the Blessed Land, reading the core rules of his territory expansion.

’The trait literally bans men from my base,’ Silas realized in horror. ’If I capture an Alpha male wolf and try to drag it back through the gates of the Keep, is the system going to register it as a male entity? Is it going to trigger a territorial violation and instantly smite the wolf to ash? Or worse, will it penalize my territory for breaking the core rule?!’
He couldn’t risk it.

If he spent all this time building a Beast Pavilion and hyping up a cavalry unit, only for the system to obliterate his mounts the second they crossed the threshold, Reina’s heart would break and he would look like a complete idiot.

’System,’ Silas thought urgently, projecting his mental query directly into the Warlord interface floating in the back of his mind. ’Clarification required... Does the territorial ban on male recruits apply to non-humanoid beasts and monster mounts?’
For two agonizing seconds, nothing happened.
Then, a crisp, glowing blue tab materialized directly in the center of his vision.
[System Query Acknowledged.]
[Processing Territorial Parameters...]

[Answer: Negative. The territory trait restriction applies strictly to Humanoid, Sentient, and Demi-Human male entities capable of holding command, hero, or troop designations. Beast-class entities, mounts, livestock, and non-sentient familiars are classified as ’Territorial Assets’ and are fully exempt from gender-based summoning/housing restrictions. Male mounts may be safely added to the Blessed Land.]
Silas let out a massive shuddering sigh of pure relief, closing his eyes for a second as the blue text faded from his vision.
’Thank God,’ Silas muttered internally. ’I thought I was going to have to run an entire cavalry unit entirely on angry female wolves.’
"Is everything alright, My Lord?" Reina asked softly, noticing him stop.
Silas opened his eyes and offered her a quick, reassuring nod.
"Everything is fine. The plan is solid. We secure the females, the cubs, and the Alpha male. We can proceed."
They crept forward for another ten minutes, following the bloody trail as it grew thicker and more chaotic.
The air in the forest grew incredibly heavy as the suffocating scent of decay mixed violently with the sharp tang of fresh blood.
Suddenly, a massive, deafening roar echoed through the dark canopy ahead.
It wasn’t the high-pitched echoing howl of a wolf.
It was a deep bone-rattling roar that sounded like a mountain tearing itself apart.
The roar was immediately followed by a chorus of desperate, vicious canine snarls and the sickening sound of heavy impacts.
"Down!" Reina hissed, dropping flat into the wet ferns.

Silas, Brida, Aeliana, and the junior squad hit the dirt instantly, crawling on their stomachs through the wet mud until they reached the edge of a steep, rocky ridge overlooking a small, sunken clearing.
Silas slowly pushed a heavy fern aside and peered down into the basin.
The scene below them was an absolute bloodbath.
Built into the side of a massive rocky cliff face was a small, dark cavern. The entrance was narrow, choked with heavy roots, but Silas could clearly see movement inside the dark opening.
Two female Umbral Wolves... massive beasts the size of draft horses, their fur a sleek dark midnight black were standing side-by-side inside the cave mouth.
Their teeth were bared in fierce, defensive snarls, and tucked safely behind their legs, whimpering in terror, were three tiny, trembling black wolf pups.
Two more female wolves were stationed just outside the cave entrance, their backs pressed against the rock wall, refusing to give an inch of ground as they protected the den.
But the real massacre was happening in the center of the clearing.
The muddy ground was completely torn apart, littered with uprooted trees and massive craters.
Lying dead in the dirt were the massive broken corpses of four Tier 2 Blood-Mane Grizzlies.
The bears were gargantuan... easily twelve feet tall, covered in thick, matted brown fur and plated with jagged bone armor across their skulls and shoulders.
The wolves had managed to kill four of them, but the cost had been devastating.
Fighting desperately in the center of the clearing against the fifth and final Blood-Mane Grizzly were the two male Umbral Wolves.
One was a younger male, clearly exhausted, limping heavily on a shattered back leg, its midnight fur soaked in its own blood.
The other was the Alpha.
The Alpha was a magnificent terrifying monster.
It was twenty percent larger than the females, its dark fur pulsing with faint streaks of violent purple umbral energy but the Alpha was losing.
Its left eye was swollen shut, its flank was torn open by deep, horrific claw marks, and its breathing was quite wet.
The fifth Grizzly was a nightmare.
It was completely untouched.

The massive bear stood on its hind legs, towering over the wolves, its rusted-iron claws dripping with blood, thick saliva frothing from its terrifying maw. It let out another bone-shaking roar, stepping forward to crush the wolves and raid the den.

"It’s a raid..." Reina whispered in horror, her eyes wide as she watched the slaughter from the ridge. "The bears are trying to eat the pups and the males are fighting to the death to buy the females time to run."
Down in the clearing, the fight erupted again with brutal violence.
The young male wolf lunged forward in a desperate, suicidal attempt to distract the bear, snapping its jaws toward the Grizzly’s hamstring.

"The girls on laundry duty said they wash your shirts, and they’re always completely shredded...

"Not flexing."
"Speaking of the Keep..." Kaal leaned forward, a devious inappropriate smirk spreading across her face.
She lowered her voice to a conspiratorial whisper.
"We all know the commanders have their own private washrooms up there but the rumor in the barracks is that the Lord doesn’t bathe alone.
Is it true you share the tub with the Goddess and the Pirate Queen?"
The entire squad of junior girls gasped, a collective scandalous giggle erupting from the middle of the formation.
A few of them blushed furiously, turning their heads away, while the bolder ones stared directly at Silas’s broad back, desperately waiting for him to answer the perverted question.
Silas closed his eyes for a fraction of a second, feeling a massive, throbbing headache forming right behind his temples.
’I am trying to run a professional military operation...’ Silas thought, groaning internally. ’And my troops are acting like a bunch of high schoolers at a sleepover.
This base has zero HR oversight.’
Before Silas could formulate a proper socially acceptable response that would shut the rumors down without causing a riot, a muscular arm violently wrapped around his bicep.
Brida stepped aggressively into the center of the formation.

The towering commander didn’t just hook his arm... she yanked Silas firmly against her side, pressing the heavy, dense muscle of her shoulder and the soft swell of her massive chest directly against his ribcage.
She glared over her shoulder at the squad of giggling recruits as her stormy eyes flashed with fierce possessiveness.
"Alright, back off, you nosy little grunts..." Brida barked, her booming voice completely devoid of any real anger, but dripping with smug superiority.
"The Boss’s bathing habits are strictly classified command business and even if he did share a tub, you lot aren’t high enough level to earn a spot in the water."
She squeezed Silas’s arm tighter, leaning her head against his shoulder and offering the junior girls a wicked, highly arrogant grin.
"Besides," Brida boasted, puffing her chest out.
"The Captain is busy today.
He’s my personal escort for this raid...
He’s mine for the afternoon, so keep your perverted questions to yourselves and keep your eyes on the trees before a swamp-troll eats you."
The junior girls immediately erupted into a chorus of disappointed groans and jealous complaints.
"That’s so unfair, Commander!" Vala whined, pouting.
"You get to hang out with him all the time during raids!"
"Yeah, stop hogging the Lord!" Kaal grumbled, crossing her arms.
"We want a turn to hold his arm!"
"Rank has its privileges, ladies!" Brida laughed loudly, completely ignoring their complaints and refusing to let go of Silas’s bicep.
Silas just sighed, shaking his head.

If letting Brida cling to his arm kept the recruits from asking any more highly invasive questions about his private life, he was perfectly fine being used as a piece of armed arm-candy for the afternoon.
"Quiet."

The playful joking atmosphere in the squad vanished in a single microsecond.

He gently untangled his arm from Brida’s grip, stepping forward with his hand dropping back to his sword hilt.

Reina motioned for him to come closer.
Silas stepped up to the Beast Tamer.
Reina pointed to the thick moss-covered trunk of a massive ironwood tree directly to their left.
Splattered across the dark green moss, roughly four feet off the ground, was a massive, fresh streak of thick dark crimson blood.
"The tracks changed," Reina whispered tightly.

Deep gouges tearing the roots up, overlapping footprints and scuff marks indicating something heavy was dragging its back legs."

Silas nodded with a sigh.
