chapters.title: Chapter 124: Drawing Aggro [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The bear didn’t even flinch.
It easily absorbed the bite against its thick fat-layered hide, spun around with terrifying speed and backhanded the young wolf with a massive, bone-plated paw.
CRACK!
The impact sounded like a cannon going off.
The crushing weight of the bear’s strike sent the young wolf flying through the air like a broken toy.
It slammed brutally against the rocky cliff face, crumbling to the ground in a motionless bloody heap.
The female wolves outside the cave let out a deafening howl of grief.
The Alpha male didn’t retreat.
Seeing its packmate fall, the Alpha surged forward, pushing its exhausted, bleeding muscles past their physical limit.
The purple umbral energy flared brilliantly across its fur as it launched itself into the air, aiming a fatal bite directly at the Grizzly’s exposed throat.
It was a perfect strike...
But the bear was simply too big and too heavy.
The Grizzly raised its massive armored forearm, catching the Alpha out of mid-air.
The bear’s rusted-iron claws dug deep into the wolf’s shoulder, completely stopping its momentum.
"GRAH!"
With a roar, the Grizzly lifted the struggling, snarling Alpha high above its head and violently slammed the wolf straight down into the solid bedrock of the clearing.
SNAP!
A sickening crunch echoed through the basin as the Alpha’s ribs shattered under the crushing force.
The wolf bounced off the stone, a spray of dark blood erupting from its mouth, and collapsed into the mud.
The Alpha tried to stand, its claws scrambling weakly against the dirt, but its legs gave out.
It collapsed back into the muck, wheezing wetly, hovering right on the brink of death.
"GRAH!"
The Grizzly let out a triumphant roar, dropping down onto all fours and slowly lumbering toward the cave entrance, its eyes locked onto the whimpering pups.
Up on the ridge, the squad watched in horrified silence. Reina was completely frozen, her hands trembling as she clutched the snare ropes.
The pack she needed... the majestic proud animals she had dreamed of taming was being butchered right in front of her eyes.
A heavy, calloused hand violently shoved Reina’s shoulder, knocking her entirely out of her paralyzed stupor.
Reina gasped, looking over.
Brida was crouching next to her, the woman’s stormy eyes burning with intense aggression.
The commander had her massive battleaxe gripped tight in both hands, the gravity runes on the heavy shaft already humming with violent suppressed power.
Brida didn’t look at the dying wolves.
She looked directly at the Beast Tamer.
"Reina," Brida demanded, her voice tight with the desperate, adrenaline-fueled need to drop into the clearing and start swinging. "What should we do?"
The heavy stench of wet rot and fresh blood hung thick in the damp air of the Unknown Zone.
Up on the muddy ridge, hidden behind a dense cluster of massive ironwood ferns, the squad lay flat on their stomachs.
Below them, the sunken clearing had been turned into a horrific violent slaughterhouse.
The massive, twenty-foot-tall Blood-Mane Grizzly roared, its rusted-iron claws dripping with dark crimson as it stood over the broken, shattered body of the Alpha Umbral Wolf.
The remaining female wolves backed against the dark cave entrance, snarling desperately to protect the whimpering pups hidden behind their legs.
Reina stared down at the carnage, her ash-blonde braid plastered to her sweating neck.
Her Beast Tamer class didn’t just give her the ability to throw snares... it gave her a deep instinctual read on animal behavior.
As she watched the bloody scene below, her mind rapidly processed the raw data of the wild.
This wasn’t a standard monster encounter.
When beasts fought for territory or food, they fought with pure aggression but the wolves down in the mud weren’t fighting for territory.
Their fur was standing straight up, their ears were pinned flat against their skulls, and their snarling was laced with a high-pitched frequency.
They were fighting out of pure terror.
They were parents making a suicidal final stand to keep a nightmare away from their den.
Reina’s eyes darted from the dying Alpha male, to the younger brother bleeding out against the rocks, to the towering bear taking a heavy step toward the cave.
If that bear reached the females, the entire bloodline would be wiped out in less than a minute.
Her analysis snapped into sharp focus.
The conclusion was instant.

"We need to help them. Right now," Reina whispered fiercely, turning her head to look at Silas and Brida. "But we cannot go in there swinging wildly. If the heavy hitters drop into that basin and start crushing things, the wolves are going to think we’re just a bigger, deadlier boss monster coming to finish the job. They’ll panic and attack us too."
She pointed a dirt-smudged finger directly at the towering Grizzly.
"We engage the bear," Reina ordered with her voice becoming very. "Only the bear. Nobody touches the wolves."
Silas nodded, his instincts instantly recognizing the soundness of her plan.
He shifted his weight, preparing to push himself up from the mud and draw his new hand-and-a-half sword.
Before Silas could move, Brida threw a muscular arm across his chest, stopping him flat in the dirt.
"Hold on a second, My Lord," Brida grinned, a wicked entertained spark lighting up her stormy eyes.
She looked past Silas and locked her gaze onto the junior infantry girls lying in the brush. She singled out the swordswoman, Vala, and the archer, Elara.
"You two," Brida commanded, pointing a thick finger at them.
Vala and Elara flinched, their eyes going wide.

"The Boss and I have been carrying you through the mud all afternoon," Brida told them with her tone changing into that of a strict expectant commander. "You want to prove you deserve to wear the territorial crest? You want to show us the fruits of your training? Get down there and take the aggro off those wolves."
Vala swallowed hard, looking down at the massive armored bear.
It was a Tier 2 monster, easily weighing over two tons, with bone plating thick enough to deflect standard arrows but she didn’t hesitate.
She was a shieldmaiden of the Blessed Land. She drew her shortsword, the steel scraping softly against the leather scabbard.
Elara didn’t back down either.
The young archer reached over her shoulder and unslung the brand new, compact tactical recurve bow she had just assembled in the forge last week.
She pulled a heavy, steel-tipped arrow from her quiver and nocked it to the spider-silk string.
"We’ve got this, Commander," Vala whispered, her hands gripping her hilt so tight her knuckles turned white.
"Make it quick," Silas told them, keeping his golden-ringed eyes locked on the bear. "If you lose the advantage, fall back instantly. I’ll cover your retreat."
Vala and Elara didn’t waste another second.
They pushed themselves up from the ferns, scrambled over the edge of the rocky ridge, and slid rapidly down the steep muddy embankment directly into the sunken clearing.
Their boots hit the wet bedrock with a loud splash.
The Blood-Mane Grizzly stopped its advance toward the cave.
The massive beast slowly turned its gargantuan, bone-plated head, its beady bloodshot eyes locking onto the two tiny human girls who had just dropped into its hunting ground.
The bear opened its jaws, letting out a deafening wet roar that blew a foul wave of rotting breath across the clearing.
Vala didn’t freeze. She remembered the harsh, brutal sparring lessons Morwenna had drilled into the infantry all week.
’Don’t let the enemy dictate the pacing... Take the space.’
"Hey! Ugly!" Vala screamed at the top of her lungs, stepping boldly into the center of the mud to draw the monster’s full attention away from the bleeding wolves.
She didn’t just yell. She planted her boots wide, turned her hip, and aggressively slapped her own canvas-clad ass with her free hand.
She stuck her tongue out, pulling her eyelid down in a universally mocking disrespectful gesture.
"Come get a piece of this, you overgrown rug!" Vala taunted loudly.
Up on the ridge, the rest of the Vanguard squad stared in stunned silence at the sheer audacity of the taunt.
Down in the mud, Elara was already moving.
The young archer sprinted to the right flank, finding a solid patch of dry rock to plant her boots.
She raised her short bow, drawing the spider-silk string back to her cheek.
"Careful, Vala!" Elara yelled across the clearing with a fierce reckless grin on her face as she lined up her shot. "He can’t have your ass! It already belongs to the Lord!"
Up on the ridge, Brida let out a massive booming bark of laughter, slapping her thigh.
Aeliana’s silver eyes widened in shock at the scandalous quip, while Silas just pinched the bridge of his nose with a deeply amused sigh escaping his chest.
Vala’s face flushed a violent shade of crimson at her friend’s public joke, but she didn’t break her stance.
The Blood-Mane Grizzly didn’t care about the banter. The insult registered as a direct territorial challenge.
The bear abandoned the wolves completely, dropping onto all fours and charging straight at Vala like a runaway freight train covered in fur and bone.
The ground physically shook under the monster’s immense weight and mud flew into the air as the rusted-iron claws tore the earth apart.
THWIP!
Elara released her bowstring.
The high-tension ironwood limbs snapped forward with terrifying velocity.
The heavy steel-tipped arrow screamed through the damp air and slammed directly into the thick fleshy gap between the bear’s shoulder bone-plates.
"GAH!"
The Grizzly roared in pain, but the momentum of its charge didn’t slow down an inch.
Vala took a deep breath.
She didn’t have an elemental affinity.
She couldn’t summon fire or throw waves of heavy ocean water like the commanders. All she had was her raw mana pool and the heavy steel in her hands.
’But that’s enough...’
She visualized her mana circuit, pushing a concentrated surge of pure, non-elemental energy down her arms and directly into the blade of her shortsword.
The steel ignited with a vibrating white hum, increasing the sharpness and durability of the edge.
The bear was five yards away.
It reared up onto its hind legs, towering twelve feet in the air, and brought its massive right paw down in a devastating crushing swipe aimed directly at Vala’s skull.
Vala didn’t block.
Blocking a two-ton bear would shatter her collarbones instantly.
She used Morwenna’s footwork.
She pivoted sharply on her left heel, dropping her center of gravity and sliding smoothly to the outside of the bear’s arc.
The rusted-iron claws missed her face by less than two inches with the wind of the strike whipping her dark hair wildly.
BOOM!
As the bear’s arm crashed into the mud beside her, Vala struck.
She drove her mana-coated shortsword in a sharp upward horizontal slash, aiming for the exposed tendons behind the beast’s knee joint.
The humming steel bit deep into the thick muscle, drawing a heavy spray of dark blood.
The Grizzly bellowed, staggering sideways as its leg briefly gave out.
It quickly recovered, spinning its massive bulk around with terrifying agility and snapping its jaws toward Vala’s torso.
THWIP! THWIP!
Elara was a machine.
The compact bow allowed her to draw and fire with blinding speed. Two arrows slammed directly into the thick, sensitive flesh of the bear’s snout, burying themselves deep into the cartilage.
The Grizzly flailed wildly, distracted and blinded by the pain, swiping its massive claws at the air.
"Keep hitting the joints!" Vala yelled, ducking under a wild chaotic swing.
She darted forward, her boots sliding in the slick mud.
She channeled another burst of raw mana into her blade, stepping directly inside the monster’s guard.
Vala didn’t aim for the thick bone plates on the chest, instead he drove the sword straight into the soft unprotected armpit of the beast, twisting the hilt violently to maximize the tissue damage.
The bear shrieked, a deafening sound that rattled the stones of the cave. It dropped its heavy bulk downward, trying to crush the swordswoman under its chest.
"Nice try fucker!"
Vala ripped her blade free and threw herself backward, rolling through the wet mud to avoid being flattened into paste.
She scrambled back to her feet with her canvas uniform completely soaked in muck and monster blood and her chest heaving as she gripped her sword.
"Keep attacking me... it helps me look cool for my Lord yunno."

With a roar, the Grizzly lifted the struggling, snarling Alpha high above its head and violently slammed the wolf straight down into the solid bedrock of the clearing.
SNAP!
A sickening crunch echoed through the basin as the Alpha’s ribs shattered under the crushing force.
The wolf bounced off the stone, a spray of dark blood erupting from its mouth, and collapsed into the mud.
The Alpha tried to stand, its claws scrambling weakly against the dirt, but its legs gave out.
It collapsed back into the muck, wheezing wetly, hovering right on the brink of death.
"GRAH!"
The Grizzly let out a triumphant roar, dropping down onto all fours and slowly lumbering toward the cave entrance, its eyes locked onto the whimpering pups.
Up on the ridge, the squad watched in horrified silence.
Reina was completely frozen, her hands trembling as she clutched the snare ropes.
The pack she needed... the majestic proud animals she had dreamed of taming was being butchered right in front of her eyes.
A heavy, calloused hand violently shoved Reina’s shoulder, knocking her entirely out of her paralyzed stupor.
Reina gasped, looking over.
Brida was crouching next to her, the woman’s stormy eyes burning with intense aggression.
The commander had her massive battleaxe gripped tight in both hands, the gravity runes on the heavy shaft already humming with violent suppressed power.
Brida didn’t look at the dying wolves.
She looked directly at the Beast Tamer.
"Reina," Brida demanded, her voice tight with the desperate, adrenaline-fueled need to drop into the clearing and start swinging.
"What should we do?"
The heavy stench of wet rot and fresh blood hung thick in the damp air of the Unknown Zone.
Up on the muddy ridge, hidden behind a dense cluster of massive ironwood ferns, the squad lay flat on their stomachs.
Below them, the sunken clearing had been turned into a horrific violent slaughterhouse.
The massive, twenty-foot-tall Blood-Mane Grizzly roared, its rusted-iron claws dripping with dark crimson as it stood over the broken, shattered body of the Alpha Umbral Wolf.
The remaining female wolves backed against the dark cave entrance, snarling desperately to protect the whimpering pups hidden behind their legs.
Reina stared down at the carnage, her ash-blonde braid plastered to her sweating neck.
Her Beast Tamer class didn’t just give her the ability to throw snares... it gave her a deep instinctual read on animal behavior.
As she watched the bloody scene below, her mind rapidly processed the raw data of the wild.
This wasn’t a standard monster encounter.
When beasts fought for territory or food, they fought with pure aggression but the wolves down in the mud weren’t fighting for territory.
Their fur was standing straight up, their ears were pinned flat against their skulls, and their snarling was laced with a high-pitched frequency.
They were fighting out of pure terror.
They were parents making a suicidal final stand to keep a nightmare away from their den.
Reina’s eyes darted from the dying Alpha male, to the younger brother bleeding out against the rocks, to the towering bear taking a heavy step toward the cave.
If that bear reached the females, the entire bloodline would be wiped out in less than a minute.
Her analysis snapped into sharp focus.
The conclusion was instant.
"We need to help them.
Right now," Reina whispered fiercely, turning her head to look at Silas and Brida.
"But we cannot go in there swinging wildly.
If the heavy hitters drop into that basin and start crushing things, the wolves are going to think we’re just a bigger, deadlier boss monster coming to finish the job.
They’ll panic and attack us too."
She pointed a dirt-smudged finger directly at the towering Grizzly.
"We engage the bear," Reina ordered with her voice becoming very.
"Only the bear.
Nobody touches the wolves."
Silas nodded, his instincts instantly recognizing the soundness of her plan.
He shifted his weight, preparing to push himself up from the mud and draw his new hand-and-a-half sword.
Before Silas could move, Brida threw a muscular arm across his chest, stopping him flat in the dirt.
"Hold on a second, My Lord," Brida grinned, a wicked entertained spark lighting up her stormy eyes.
She looked past Silas and locked her gaze onto the junior infantry girls lying in the brush.
She singled out the swordswoman, Vala, and the archer, Elara.
"You two," Brida commanded, pointing a thick finger at them.
Vala and Elara flinched, their eyes going wide.
"The Boss and I have been carrying you through the mud all afternoon," Brida told them with her tone changing into that of a strict expectant commander.
"You want to prove you deserve to wear the territorial crest?
You want to show us the fruits of your training?
Get down there and take the aggro off those wolves."
Vala swallowed hard, looking down at the massive armored bear.
It was a Tier 2 monster, easily weighing over two tons, with bone plating thick enough to deflect standard arrows but she didn’t hesitate.
She was a shieldmaiden of the Blessed Land.
She drew her shortsword, the steel scraping softly against the leather scabbard.
Elara didn’t back down either.
The young archer reached over her shoulder and unslung the brand new, compact tactical recurve bow she had just assembled in the forge last week.
She pulled a heavy, steel-tipped arrow from her quiver and nocked it to the spider-silk string.
"We’ve got this, Commander," Vala whispered, her hands gripping her hilt so tight her knuckles turned white.
"Make it quick," Silas told them, keeping his golden-ringed eyes locked on the bear.
"If you lose the advantage, fall back instantly.
I’ll cover your retreat."
Vala and Elara didn’t waste another second.
They pushed themselves up from the ferns, scrambled over the edge of the rocky ridge, and slid rapidly down the steep muddy embankment directly into the sunken clearing.
Their boots hit the wet bedrock with a loud splash.
The Blood-Mane Grizzly stopped its advance toward the cave.
The massive beast slowly turned its gargantuan, bone-plated head, its beady bloodshot eyes locking onto the two tiny human girls who had just dropped into its hunting ground.
The bear opened its jaws, letting out a deafening wet roar that blew a foul wave of rotting breath across the clearing.
Vala didn’t freeze.
She remembered the harsh, brutal sparring lessons Morwenna had drilled into the infantry all week.
’Don’t let the enemy dictate the pacing...
Take the space.’
"Hey!
Ugly!" Vala screamed at the top of her lungs, stepping boldly into the center of the mud to draw the monster’s full attention away from the bleeding wolves.
She didn’t just yell.
She planted her boots wide, turned her hip, and aggressively slapped her own canvas-clad ass with her free hand.
She stuck her tongue out, pulling her eyelid down in a universally mocking disrespectful gesture.
"Come get a piece of this, you overgrown rug!" Vala taunted loudly.
Up on the ridge, the rest of the Vanguard squad stared in stunned silence at the sheer audacity of the taunt.
Down in the mud, Elara was already moving.
The young archer sprinted to the right flank, finding a solid patch of dry rock to plant her boots.
She raised her short bow, drawing the spider-silk string back to her cheek.
"Careful, Vala!" Elara yelled across the clearing with a fierce reckless grin on her face as she lined up her shot.
"He can’t have your ass!
It already belongs to the Lord!"
Up on the ridge, Brida let out a massive booming bark of laughter, slapping her thigh.
Aeliana’s silver eyes widened in shock at the scandalous quip, while Silas just pinched the bridge of his nose with a deeply amused sigh escaping his chest.
Vala’s face flushed a violent shade of crimson at her friend’s public joke, but she didn’t break her stance.
The Blood-Mane Grizzly didn’t care about the banter.
The insult registered as a direct territorial challenge.
The bear abandoned the wolves completely, dropping onto all fours and charging straight at Vala like a runaway freight train covered in fur and bone.
The ground physically shook under the monster’s immense weight and mud flew into the air as the rusted-iron claws tore the earth apart.
THWIP!
Elara released her bowstring.
The high-tension ironwood limbs snapped forward with terrifying velocity.
The heavy steel-tipped arrow screamed through the damp air and slammed directly into the thick fleshy gap between the bear’s shoulder bone-plates.
"GAH!"
The Grizzly roared in pain, but the momentum of its charge didn’t slow down an inch.
Vala took a deep breath.
She didn’t have an elemental affinity.
She couldn’t summon fire or throw waves of heavy ocean water like the commanders.
All she had was her raw mana pool and the heavy steel in her hands.
’But that’s enough...’
She visualized her mana circuit, pushing a concentrated surge of pure, non-elemental energy down her arms and directly into the blade of her shortsword.
The steel ignited with a vibrating white hum, increasing the sharpness and durability of the edge.
The bear was five yards away.
It reared up onto its hind legs, towering twelve feet in the air, and brought its massive right paw down in a devastating crushing swipe aimed directly at Vala’s skull.
Vala didn’t block.
Blocking a two-ton bear would shatter her collarbones instantly.
She used Morwenna’s footwork.
She pivoted sharply on her left heel, dropping her center of gravity and sliding smoothly to the outside of the bear’s arc.
The rusted-iron claws missed her face by less than two inches with the wind of the strike whipping her dark hair wildly.
BOOM!
As the bear’s arm crashed into the mud beside her, Vala struck.
She drove her mana-coated shortsword in a sharp upward horizontal slash, aiming for the exposed tendons behind the beast’s knee joint.
The humming steel bit deep into the thick muscle, drawing a heavy spray of dark blood.
The Grizzly bellowed, staggering sideways as its leg briefly gave out.
It quickly recovered, spinning its massive bulk around with terrifying agility and snapping its jaws toward Vala’s torso.
THWIP!
THWIP!
Elara was a machine.
The compact bow allowed her to draw and fire with blinding speed.
Two arrows slammed directly into the thick, sensitive flesh of the bear’s snout, burying themselves deep into the cartilage.
The Grizzly flailed wildly, distracted and blinded by the pain, swiping its massive claws at the air.
"Keep hitting the joints!" Vala yelled, ducking under a wild chaotic swing.
She darted forward, her boots sliding in the slick mud.
She channeled another burst of raw mana into her blade, stepping directly inside the monster’s guard.
Vala didn’t aim for the thick bone plates on the chest, instead he drove the sword straight into the soft unprotected armpit of the beast, twisting the hilt violently to maximize the tissue damage.
The bear shrieked, a deafening sound that rattled the stones of the cave.
It dropped its heavy bulk downward, trying to crush the swordswoman under its chest.
"Nice try fucker!"
Vala ripped her blade free and threw herself backward, rolling through the wet mud to avoid being flattened into paste.
She scrambled back to her feet with her canvas uniform completely soaked in muck and monster blood and her chest heaving as she gripped her sword.
"Keep attacking me... it helps me look cool for my Lord yunno."

chapters.title: Chapter 125: The Ultimatum [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The Grizzly was severely wounded, bleeding heavily from its knee, its armpit, and its snout but it was far from dead.
Driven into a frenzy of pain and rage, the monster locked its remaining good eye onto Elara.
It ignored the swordswoman and charged the archer.
"Hey, come back!"
Elara didn’t panic.
She stood her ground on the rock, calmly pulling another arrow from her quiver.
’Like Fenna taught me...’
Elara tracked the bouncing uneven gait of the charging beast. She didn’t aim for the chest as she instead aimed for the tiny dark target of its remaining eye.
She drew the string to her cheek.
She exhaled.
THWIP!
The arrow flew true. It punched cleanly through the soft tissue of the bear’s eye socket, sinking deep into the skull.
The Grizzly’s brain scrambled.
The massive monster let out a garbled wet choking sound, its front legs collapsing underneath its immense weight.
The bear crashed face-first into the mud, sliding forward from its own momentum, tearing a deep trench in the earth as it skidded to a halt just ten feet away from the archer.
It tried to push itself back up with its claws scraping uselessly against the bedrock but Vala wasn’t going to give it the chance.
The swordswoman sprinted across the clearing.
She didn’t slow down as she reached the downed beast.
"Get over here!" She planted her boot directly onto the bear’s massive bone-plated shoulder, using the monster’s own body as a stepping stool to launch herself into the air.
At the apex of her jump, Vala poured every single drop of her remaining non-elemental mana into her shortsword.

The blade flared with a brilliant blinding white hum as she brought the sword down in a devastating two-handed vertical strike, driving the humming steel directly into the back of the Grizzly’s thick neck, aiming straight for the gap in the cervical vertebrae.
The steel crunched through bone and severed the spinal cord.
The massive Blood-Mane Grizzly went completely limp. Its heavy head slammed back into the mud with a wet thud, and it stopped moving entirely.
Total silence fell over the bloody clearing, broken only by the ragged panting of the two junior recruits.
Vala stood on the back of the dead bear, her hands trembling as she slowly pulled her sword free from the monster’s neck.
She looked across the mud at Elara. The archer lowered her bow, offering a tired shaky grin.
"Weapons down!" Reina’s voice rang out from the ridge above. "Keep your hands open and away from your hilts!"
Vala immediately sheathed her shortsword, sliding off the bear’s corpse.
Elara slung her bow over her shoulder. Both girls raised their empty hands, making sure they didn’t look like a threat to the terrified wolves huddled near the cave.
Up on the embankment, the rest of the squad stood up from the ferns.
They slid down the muddy slope with boots hitting the basin floor.
Brida walked with a wide grin of pure pride on her face, while Silas led the girls, his own dark sword securely sheathed at his hip.
Silas walked straight past the dead Grizzly, stopping in front of the two sweating, exhausted junior girls.

"Flawless footwork, Vala," Silas praised her genuinely with his deep voice carrying a tone of approval. "You didn’t fight the weight of the beast, rather you redirected it. Morwenna’s lessons paid off... That was top-tier combat."
Vala’s chest puffed out, a massive, proud smile breaking through the mud and sweat on her face. "Thank you, Lord Graves!"
Silas turned his head with his golden-ringed eyes shifting to the young archer. He offered Elara a slow amused smirk.

"And for the record, Elara," Silas said dryly, crossing his arms over his armored chest. "It’s very good to know that my scouts are guarding my territorial assets with such fierce dedicated enthusiasm."
Elara’s face instantly turned the color of a ripe tomato.
The adrenaline of the fight crashed, leaving her standing in front of her Lord after publicly screaming a degenerate joke about another girl’s backside belonging to him.
"I... I was just trying to draw aggro, My Lord!" Elara stammered, frantically waving her hands while Brida cackled loudly in the background. "It was a taunt! I swear!"
"It worked," Silas chuckled, letting her off the hook. He turned his attention away from the junior girls and looked toward the far side of the clearing.
The real test was just beginning.
Reina stepped forward, moving slowly and deliberately past the squad.
The Alpha male Umbral Wolf was lying in the mud, its chest heaving with shallow agonizing breaths.
Its ribs were completely shattered, its left eye swollen shut, and dark blood pooled beneath its torn flank.
Despite its fatal injuries, the massive beast tried to raise its head as Reina approached, letting out a weak defensive snarl.
Over by the cave, the females tensed, baring their teeth, ready to fight to the death if the humans took one more step toward the pups.
Reina didn’t draw a weapon. She didn’t carry a whip or a heavy chain.
She slowly sank down to her knees in the wet mud, making herself look as small and unthreatening as physically possible. She held her bare hands out with palms facing upward.
She tapped deep into her Beast Tamer class skills, projecting a dense aura of pure empathetic calm across the clearing.
"Easy," Reina spoke softly.
She didn’t use harsh grunts or clicks.

She spoke in clear, calm human language, letting the magical resonance of her voice convey her intent. "We aren’t here for your den. The bear is dead and the hunt is over. We aren’t going to hurt your family."
The Alpha’s ears twitched. The fierce, desperate snarling slowly faded into a low rumbling growl of pure exhaustion, though its one good eye remained locked onto her with heavy suspicion.
While Reina held the Alpha’s attention, Silas moved.

He didn’t walk toward the Alpha or the females. He walked in a wide, slow arc around the edge of the clearing, heading straight for the rocky cliff face where the younger brother wolf was lying motionless in a pile of bloody rubble.
The Alpha realized what the Lord was doing.
It tried to snap its jaws, struggling to push itself up from the mud to defend its brother, but its shattered ribs gave out.
The massive wolf collapsed back into the dirt, watching helplessly as the tall human approached its kin.
Silas reached the younger wolf. The beast was barely breathing, its back leg twisted at a horrifying unnatural angle.
Silas didn’t hesitate. He dropped to one knee beside the dying monster as he pulled off his heavy leather right glove, exposing his bare skin.
He placed his open palm directly onto the wolf’s blood-soaked flank.
The Alpha let out a desperate warning bark but Silas ignored it. He focused his mind, drawing power from the very center of his Gold Core and funneling it straight into the back of his right hand.
The Genesis Rune burned to life.
A brilliant blinding array of complex green lines and geometric shapes ignited across Silas’s knuckles.
In the blink of an eye, a massive flood of pure, warm, life-giving green light poured out of the rune and washed completely over the shattered body of the young wolf.
The magic was immediate and miraculous.
The sickening sound of bones snapping back into proper alignment echoed softly through the clearing.
The deep lacerations across the wolf’s fur physically knit themselves back together, closing up without leaving a single scar.
The twisted back leg straightened out, the tendons reattaching and strengthening under the green glow.
In less than five seconds, the young wolf’s shallow breathing deepened into strong healthy lungfuls of air.
The green light faded, leaving the clearing in dim shadows once again.
The young male wolf’s eyes snapped open. It let out a startled yelp, scrambling to its feet.
It didn’t limp or bleed. Instead it stood perfectly upright on all four legs, looking down at its own body in pure canine confusion.
The Alpha stared at its brother, completely stunned.
The female wolves near the cave stopped snarling entirely, their ears perking up in disbelief.

"See?" Reina continued her calm soothing dialogue, keeping her hands open toward the Alpha. "We didn’t come to kill... You fought hard and you protected your pack but you don’t have to fight like this anymore."
She slowly stood up from the mud, keeping her movements smooth and predictable.
"You don’t have to bleed for scraps in the dark," Reina told the dying pack leader. "Our territory has walls... It has warmth... It has stone to sleep on during the rain and we have premium meat."
She turned her head slightly and gave Silas a sharp nod.
Silas understood the assignment. He tapped his Warlord interface, opening his Lord Inventory.
He didn’t pull out the raw bloody cuts of monster meat he normally carried for the forge.
He definitely didn’t pull out Umbral Wolf meat either.
He selected the premium, high-quality roasted boar flanks that Kaalia had prepared back in the Keep’s kitchen.
With a flash of golden pixels, four massive steaming slabs of perfectly cooked, rich, savory boar meat materialized in Silas’s hands.
The incredible smell of roasted fat and spices instantly flooded the damp clearing, completely overpowering the stench of the dead bear.
Silas took two steps forward and tossed the heavy slabs of meat gently onto the flat, clean rocks near the center of the clearing, well within reach of the females.
For a long moment, nobody moved.
The wolves stared at the cooked meat, their noses twitching violently as the rich scent hit their starving senses.
Slowly, cautiously, one of the massive female wolves crept away from the cave entrance.
She kept her belly low to the ground with her eyes darting between Silas and Brida, expecting a trap to snap shut at any second.
She reached the rock and she sniffed the roasted boar flank.
Her hunger overrode her caution. She opened her jaws, grabbing the massive chunk of meat but she didn’t eat it herself.
She clamped her teeth around the edge of the slab, turned around, and dragged the heavy prize straight back to the cave entrance, dropping it right in front of the three tiny, trembling black pups.
The smell of the food was too much for the babies to resist.
The three tiny pups scrambled out from behind their mother’s legs, their tails tucked between their legs.
They took two bites of the roasted boar before they realized something infinitely more interesting was standing just a few feet away.
The pups completely ignored the food... They turned their heads, their tiny noses sniffing the air, and locked onto Silas.
To the shock of the entire Vanguard squad, the three tiny Umbral Wolf pups abandoned the safety of their den.
They waddled aggressively across the muddy clearing on their oversized paws, walking straight past the terrifying commander and the Arcanist, heading directly for the Lord.
Silas blinked in surprise as the three pups reached his boots.

They didn’t act like wild monsters. They acted like eager puppies. One of them immediately started chewing happily on the tough leather of his bootlaces, while the other two stood on their hind legs, whining softly and pawing at his dark canvas trousers, begging for attention.
Silas couldn’t help it.
A soft genuine smile broke across his face.
He knelt down in the mud, reaching into his inventory to pull out a few smaller, bite-sized scraps of roasted meat.
He held his hand out flat, letting the tiny apex predators happily lick the food right off his bare palm.
"Look at them," Vala cooed from the background, completely melting at the sight as she and Elara crept closer to help hand out small scraps to the babies.
Reina watched the interaction, thoroughly baffled.

’Why are the pups so attracted to him?’ Reina wondered, rubbing her forehead. ’He’s a massive armored Warlord holding a sword... He should be terrifying to them. Does he project some kind of overwhelming alpha aura that overrides their natural fear instincts?’
Whatever the reason, the sight of the Lord gently feeding the babies was the final definitive proof the pack needed to realize the humans were not a threat.
The females relaxed their posture, stepping out to claim the rest of the meat. The younger brother trotted over to join them, eating hungrily.
Reina turned her full attention back to the bleeding, shattered Alpha male lying in the dirt.
It was time for the ultimatum.
"We are going back to our sanctuary now," Reina spoke clearly, her voice ringing with the final authority of a Master Beast Tamer.
She didn’t issue a threat but instead she offered a choice.
"You can come with us. If you do, your wounds will heal. Your mate will be safe and your pups will never starve again."

He tapped his Warlord interface, opening his Lord Inventory.
He didn’t pull out the raw bloody cuts of monster meat he normally carried for the forge.
He definitely didn’t pull out Umbral Wolf meat either.
He selected the premium, high-quality roasted boar flanks that Kaalia had prepared back in the Keep’s kitchen.
With a flash of golden pixels, four massive steaming slabs of perfectly cooked, rich, savory boar meat materialized in Silas’s hands.
The incredible smell of roasted fat and spices instantly flooded the damp clearing, completely overpowering the stench of the dead bear.
Silas took two steps forward and tossed the heavy slabs of meat gently onto the flat, clean rocks near the center of the clearing, well within reach of the females.
For a long moment, nobody moved.
The wolves stared at the cooked meat, their noses twitching violently as the rich scent hit their starving senses.
Slowly, cautiously, one of the massive female wolves crept away from the cave entrance.
She kept her belly low to the ground with her eyes darting between Silas and Brida, expecting a trap to snap shut at any second.
She reached the rock and she sniffed the roasted boar flank.
Her hunger overrode her caution.
She opened her jaws, grabbing the massive chunk of meat but she didn’t eat it herself.
She clamped her teeth around the edge of the slab, turned around, and dragged the heavy prize straight back to the cave entrance, dropping it right in front of the three tiny, trembling black pups.
The smell of the food was too much for the babies to resist.
The three tiny pups scrambled out from behind their mother’s legs, their tails tucked between their legs.
They took two bites of the roasted boar before they realized something infinitely more interesting was standing just a few feet away.
The pups completely ignored the food...
They turned their heads, their tiny noses sniffing the air, and locked onto Silas.
To the shock of the entire Vanguard squad, the three tiny Umbral Wolf pups abandoned the safety of their den.
They waddled aggressively across the muddy clearing on their oversized paws, walking straight past the terrifying commander and the Arcanist, heading directly for the Lord.
Silas blinked in surprise as the three pups reached his boots.
They didn’t act like wild monsters.
They acted like eager puppies.

One of them immediately started chewing happily on the tough leather of his bootlaces, while the other two stood on their hind legs, whining softly and pawing at his dark canvas trousers, begging for attention.
Silas couldn’t help it.
A soft genuine smile broke across his face.
He knelt down in the mud, reaching into his inventory to pull out a few smaller, bite-sized scraps of roasted meat.
He held his hand out flat, letting the tiny apex predators happily lick the food right off his bare palm.
"Look at them," Vala cooed from the background, completely melting at the sight as she and Elara crept closer to help hand out small scraps to the babies.
Reina watched the interaction, thoroughly baffled.
’Why are the pups so attracted to him?’ Reina wondered, rubbing her forehead. ’He’s a massive armored Warlord holding a sword...
He should be terrifying to them.
Does he project some kind of overwhelming alpha aura that overrides their natural fear instincts?’
Whatever the reason, the sight of the Lord gently feeding the babies was the final definitive proof the pack needed to realize the humans were not a threat.
The females relaxed their posture, stepping out to claim the rest of the meat.
The younger brother trotted over to join them, eating hungrily.
Reina turned her full attention back to the bleeding, shattered Alpha male lying in the dirt.
It was time for the ultimatum.
"We are going back to our sanctuary now," Reina spoke clearly, her voice ringing with the final authority of a Master Beast Tamer.
She didn’t issue a threat but instead she offered a choice.
"You can come with us.
If you do, your wounds will heal.
Your mate will be safe and your pups will never starve again."

chapters.title: Chapter 126: Master-Slave Contract [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: She gestured to the dark oppressive treeline surrounding them.

"Or you can stay here in the wild," Reina continued smoothly. "If you reject the tether, we will pack up and walk away. We will not harm you and we will not hunt your pack. But the forest is cruel. We killed this bear, but we both know another one will come tomorrow."
She took a step back, folding her arms. "It’s your choice."
The Alpha lay in the cold wet mud.
Every single breath sent a spike of agonizing pain through his shattered ribs. The metallic taste of his own blood coated his tongue, and his vision was swimming with dark spots.
He didn’t think in complex human sentences, but his raw intelligence processed the reality of the situation with devastating clarity.
He had failed today.
He was the pack leader.

His singular purpose in the hierarchy of the wild was to protect the den, provide food, and secure the bloodline but when the massive, bone-plated monster had charged out of the trees, his fangs hadn’t been sharp enough.
His claws hadn’t been strong enough.
He had watched his younger brother get swatted against the stone like a fragile branch.
He had felt his own bones crack under the crushing weight of the bear.
If the two-legged creatures hadn’t dropped from the ridge, his mate and her sisters would be dead, and his pups would have been devoured.
The Alpha looked across the clearing through his one good eye.
He saw his brother.
The young male wasn’t a broken heap of flesh anymore.
He was standing tall, eating rich, cooked meat, completely whole thanks to the warm green light that had poured from the tall male’s hand.
He looked at his mate. She wasn’t snarling in terror as she was eating in peace instead, even glancing over to try and carry food for him.
He looked at his pups.
The tiny heirs to his bloodline were rolling around in the mud, happily chewing on the boots of the tall dark-haired male who radiated an aura of overwhelming power.
The Alpha looked back at the ash-blonde female standing in front of him.
She wasn’t aggressive.
She didn’t carry the scent of malice or the stench of a trap. She projected a calm steady feeling that felt remarkably like the protective warmth of a deep den.
His primal instincts warred with his pride.
Submitting to another creature went against every fiber of his being... Surrendering his freedom meant trusting these two-legged beings with the lives of his family.

There was always a chance this was a trick and there was a chance they would wait until his guard was down to slaughter them all but as he felt the cold wind of the Unknown Zone blow through the trees, he knew the truth.
The forest was merciless. He was broken. If he stayed here, his family would die before the sun rose again.
He took the chance.
The Alpha dug his claws deep into the mud. Ignoring the blinding agony in his chest, he forced his massive, bleeding body to rise.
His legs shook violently, his muscles trembling under his weight, but he managed to stand upright.
He looked directly at Reina, then shifted his gaze to Silas.
The massive Umbral Wolf let out a low howl that carried through the clearing.
Then, the Alpha lowered his heavy magnificent head.
He dropped his gaze to the dirt, bending his front legs until his snout physically touched the wet mud in front of Reina’s boots.
It was an gesture of total submission.
The reaction from the pack was instantaneous.
Hearing their Alpha surrender, the younger brother stopped eating. He turned toward the humans and lowered his head, bowing deeply.
The four massive females stepped away from the rocks, lowering their own heads until their snouts touched the earth.
Even the three tiny pups stopped chewing on Silas’s boots, plopping down onto their bellies and tucking their paws in.
They had given their trust to the Blessed Land...
Reina let out a long shuddering breath with a massive smile breaking across her face as the tether officially locked into her soul.
Silas stood up from the pups, brushing the dirt off his knees.
Right in the center of his vision, a bright, glowing blue holographic tab materialized.
[Territorial Event Triggered!]
[9 Umbral Wolves want to join Blessed Land as Mounts.]
[Would you like to allow? Y / N]
Silas didn’t even blink. He reached his finger out and firmly tapped the glowing blue ’Y’.
The very second his fingertip made contact with the system prompt, the air in the bloody clearing simply stopped moving.
The harsh biting wind of the Umbral Basin died instantly. The suffocating stench of rotting swamp water and dead bear was pushed away by a sudden intense wave of pure power.
Deep inside Silas’s chest, his Mythic Gold Core violently reacted to the acceptance of the tether.
He didn’t consciously channel his mana, but his body acted on its own.
A brilliant, blinding pillar of golden light erupted directly from his sternum.
The golden light shot outward in a massive expanding shockwave, completely consuming the seven kneeling Umbral Wolves.
Reina gasped, throwing her arms up to shield her eyes from the blinding glare.
Brida took a half-step back, her heavy boots sinking into the mud as the sheer pressure of the Lord’s aura washed over the clearing.
Even Aeliana had to squint, her silver eyes reflecting the intense burning gold.
Inside the pillar of light, the wolves didn’t whimper. They didn’t thrash or try to escape.
Silas watched in awe as the dark corrupted purple energy that had always clung to their midnight-black fur began to physically burn away.
The swamp grime, the matted blood, and the sickly umbral shadows were violently purged from their bodies.
As the corruption dissolved, their fur began to change.
The dark, pitch-black coats shifted, lightening rapidly until every single wolf in the pack was covered in a thick majestic coat of pure radiant gold.
The blinding light finally snapped out of existence, leaving the clearing bathed in the bruised purple sunlight of the late afternoon.
Silas lowered his arm, staring at the pack.
They didn’t look like monsters anymore... They were quite breathtaking.

The Alpha male, whose ribs had been shattered just minutes ago, now stood tall and proud, his golden fur catching the dim light, his previously swollen eye completely clear and glowing with a sharp amber hue.
The females looked like statues of carved sunlight, and the three tiny pups were essentially glowing balls of golden fluff.
[Ding!]
A rapid series of blue system notifications cascaded down the left side of Silas’s vision.
[Territorial Integration Successful!]
[Species Evolution Triggered: Corrupted Umbral Wolves have been purified.]
[New Species Registered: Blessed Wolves.]
[Pact Established: Master-Slave Territorial Contract.]
[Note: As the Sovereign Lord of the Blessed Land, you hold absolute authority over these entities. You may revoke their contract and banish them from the territory at any time.]
Silas read the prompts, letting out a slow, steady breath.

’A Master-Slave contract...’ Silas thought. ’The Sovereign realm doesn’t mess around with semantics but it makes sense. I can’t have apex predators running around my base with free will. If one of them snaps and goes feral near the junior recruits, I need the authority to shut them down instantly.’
He swiped the notifications away and looked at the golden pack standing before him.
They were staring right back at him. All seven pairs of amber eyes were locked onto his face, waiting for his command with an intense unblinking focus.
Silas cleared his throat.
He felt incredibly awkward.
He was a guy from Earth who used to work a dead-end job, and now he was standing in a swamp, preparing to give a motivational Warlord speech to a pack of glowing dogs.
’Do they even understand English?’ Silas wondered internally. ’Whatever... Just play the part and project authority.’
Silas took a step forward, resting his hands casually on his hips.

"Alright, listen up," Silas spoke, keeping his voice low and laced with the calm confidence of a commander. "The old rules of the wild are dead... You don’t belong to the Umbral Basin anymore. You belong to the Blessed Land instead. You all belong to me."
He pointed a finger down at the dead, twenty-foot-tall Blood-Mane Grizzly rotting in the mud.

"You work for my territory now, and in exchange, you never have to worry about fighting a monster like this alone ever again," Silas promised them, making sure his tone was dead serious. "No more starving in a wet cave... No more freezing in the rain... You protect my scouts, you carry my girls into battle, and my cooks will feed you premium roasted meat every single day until you’re fat and happy. Do we have a deal?"
For a second, there was total silence then, the massive golden Alpha male tilted his head back toward the purple sky.
AWOOOOOOOO!
The Alpha let out a deafening, majestic howl that rattled the leaves of the ironwood trees.
A split second later, the younger brother joined in, followed by the four massive females.
Even the three tiny pups tilted their little heads back and let out high-pitched squeaky little howls that lacked any real menace but made up for it in pure enthusiasm.
The synchronized howling echoed across the swamp, a clear undeniable acceptance of the Lord’s terms.
"I’ll take that as a yes," Silas smirked.

He turned to Reina, who was still standing near the edge of the clearing with her mouth slightly open. "Job’s done, Reina. Let’s pack it up and head home before the blood smell attracts another bear."
"Yes, My Lord!" Reina snapped a crisp salute, her heart soaring as she coiled her snare ropes back over her shoulder.
She didn’t even need to use them.
The Warlord had bypassed the entire trapping process with pure charisma.
Silas turned around, intending to take the point position and lead the squad back up the muddy ridge.
Before he could take a single step, a heavy, warm weight pressed against his left hip.
Silas stopped and looked down.
One of the massive golden females... a towering beast that stood well over five feet tall at the shoulder had trotted up beside him.

She didn’t growl, instead she simply pressed her thick muscular shoulder against his leg, let out a soft rumbling huff, and deliberately lowered her front legs, dipping her back down in a clear undeniable gesture.
Silas blinked in genuine surprise.
He looked over at Reina, raising an eyebrow. "Is she doing what I think she’s doing?"
Reina’s jaw hit the floor.
The Beast Tamer’s eyes widened to comical proportions as she stared at the female wolf offering her back to the Lord.

"She... she’s offering to carry you," Reina stammered out, completely baffled by the animal psychology playing out in front of her. "My Lord, that is unheard of. Even with a contract, wild mounts usually take weeks of saddle-drills, treats, and dominance-wrestling before they allow a rider to sit on their spine... Their protective instincts make them hate having blind spots covered but she just met you ten minutes ago."
Silas chuckled, reaching a hand out to stroke the thick golden fur behind the wolf’s ears. "I guess I just have a trustworthy face."
He didn’t want to insult the wolf by rejecting the offer.
Plus, his legs were still a bit sore.
Silas grabbed a thick handful of golden fur near the wolf’s neck, swung his long leg over her broad back, and settled himself firmly just behind her shoulder blades.
The female wolf immediately stood back up to her full height.
She didn’t buckle under his heavy weight or the extra pounds of his steel-weave armor.
She let out a happy, energetic snort with her tail wagging slightly as she shifted her paws in the mud, clearly proud to be carrying the Alpha of the two-legged pack.
"Well, don’t just stand there," Silas called out to the rest of the squad, grinning down at them from his new elevated vantage point. "Grab a ride if you want. We’ve got six more full-grown wolves."
Brida’s stormy eyes lit up like fireworks.
The brawler didn’t need to be told twice. She aggressively shoved her battleaxe onto her back and marched straight toward the younger male wolf.
"Come here, you giant dog!" Brida laughed, reaching her heavy, calloused hands out to grab the wolf’s scruff. "Let’s see how fast you can run with a real warrior on your back!"
GRRRRRR!...

chapters.title: Chapter 127: New Mounts Into Blessed Land
paragraphs: The younger male wolf instantly bared its fangs, letting out a deep vibrating warning growl that stopped Brida dead in her tracks.
The wolf didn’t snap at her, but it aggressively stepped backward, its golden fur bristling along its spine as it flatly refused to let the commander touch it.
"Hey!" Brida complained, crossing her thick arms and pouting. "What’s the big deal? You just let the Boss sit on your sister!"
Vala and Elara eagerly approached two of the other females, hoping to score a ride, but they were met with the exact same reaction.
The female wolves growled softly, dodging the girls’ hands and jogging over to stand protectively behind Silas’s mount, completely rejecting any other riders.
Even Reina, the dedicated Beast Tamer, received a firm warning huff from the Alpha male when she stepped too close.
"I don’t understand," Elara frowned, lowering her hands. "Why won’t they let us ride?"
Reina analyzed the wolves’ defensive posture with the answer clicking into place.

"It’s basic pack hierarchy," Reina explained, looking up at Silas. "They submitted to the Lord. He healed their family, he killed the bear, and his aura dominated them. In their eyes, he is the Alpha of this territory. They are honored to carry him. But the rest of us?"

She sighed, gesturing to herself and the junior squad. "To them, we are just regular pack members. We haven’t earned their respect yet so until we spend time feeding them and working with them in the Pavilion, they aren’t going to let us treat them like pack-horses."
"Tough break, ladies," Silas smirked from his comfortable perch on the golden wolf’s back. "Looks like you’re walking. Keep the pace up. I want to be back before Kaelia finishes that stew..."
The girls groaned collectively, but they fell into formation, making their way back up the muddy ridge with the golden pack of wolves trotting safely in the center of their lines.
The ride back to the Blessed Land was a completely surreal experience for Silas.
He was used to walking through the Umbral Basin with his boots constantly sinking into hidden mud pits, tripping over dark roots, and burning his stamina to stay upright.
But sitting on the back of the massive Blessed Wolf, he felt like he was floating.
The wolf’s gait was incredibly smooth.
Despite her massive size, she didn’t lumber or bounce. Her wide, padded paws hit the slick mud with total silence, absorbing the shock of the uneven terrain with flawless biological engineering.
Silas barely had to grip her fur to keep his balance; he just swayed naturally with her movements and the fur itself was astonishing.
’It’s like sitting on a mattress made of warm silk,’ Silas thought, running his bare fingers through the thick, golden coat.
It didn’t feel coarse or greasy like normal animal hair.

The evolution from the Gold Core had purified the coat, making it incredibly soft, radiating a deeply soothing warmth that seeped right through his dark canvas trousers and eased the soreness in his lower back.
As they walked, Silas absentmindedly stroked the thick fur near her shoulder blades.
Suddenly, his fingers brushed against something hard and uneven buried deep near the root of the hair.
Silas frowned. He parted the golden fur with two fingers, leaning down to inspect the anomaly.
Buried deep against the wolf’s skin was a disgusting dark gray parasite.
It looked like a cross between a bloated swamp tick and a fat, segmented leech, easily the size of a golf ball.
It had its jagged pincers dug deep into her flesh, pulsing rhythmically as it drank her blood.
’Nasty...’ Silas sneered in disgust.
He didn’t ignore it. He pinched the bloated, rubbery body of the parasite between his thumb and forefinger, gripped it tight, and gave it a sharp violent yank.
SQUELCH!
The parasite popped free from the wolf’s skin with a sickening wet tearing sound, taking a tiny drop of fresh blood with it.
The female wolf flinched, letting out a sharp high-pitched whimper of pain.
She briefly broke her stride, turning her massive golden head around to look at Silas with wide confused amber eyes, wondering why her new Alpha had just hurt her.
Silas didn’t say a word.
He just held up the writhing, disgusting gray swamp worm so she could see exactly what he had pulled off her back.
He closed his fist, crushing the parasite into a burst of foul dark fluid. He wiped the mess off his leather glove onto a passing tree trunk.
The wolf’s confusion vanished instantly. She understood exactly what he had done.
She let out a soft grateful chuff with her tail wagging wildly behind her, and she affectionately nudged her wet nose against his knee before turning forward and picking her smooth pace back up.
’Good girl,’ Silas smiled, giving her neck another firm scratch.
Down in the mud, the squad was keeping up a steady, fast-paced jog, but the banter was in full swing.
The absurdity of watching their armored Warlord riding a giant, glowing dog through a dark swamp was too much for the junior girls to ignore.

"He looks so smug up there..." Vala grumbled good-naturedly, wiping mud off her cheek as she jogged behind the wolf. "He’s not even sweating anymore. I bet he’s going to make this his permanent throne and just ride around the base inspecting us."
"I would," Elara laughed, keeping her bow steady. "If I had a golden mount that soft, my feet would never touch the dirt again."
Brida was marching on Silas’s left flank, glaring jealously at the wolf.

"I still think it’s unfair," Brida complained loudly, swinging her battleaxe like a walking stick. "I’m a commander. I should have mount privileges! Hey, Boss, tell your dog to let me sit behind you! She’s got enough room on her spine for two!"
The female wolf let out a sharp immediate growl without even looking at the woman, picking up her pace to put more distance between them.
"The lady said no, Brida," Silas chuckled, patting the wolf’s neck. "You’re too heavy anyway. You’d break her back."
"I am not heavy!" Brida yelled with her face flushing bright red. "I’m dense! It’s pure muscle mass, Captain!"
Aeliana was drifting silently on Silas’s right flank, her pristine white robes practically gliding over the mud.
The Arcanist hadn’t said a word since they left the clearing. Her glowing eyes were locked onto the female wolf Silas was currently straddling.
If looks could kill, the golden beast would have been reduced to ash an hour ago. Aeliana’s thoughts were anything but calm.

’That filthy unrefined swamp animal is carrying him,’ Aeliana thought, her delicate fingers twitching as she gripped her clipboard. ’She gets to feel the warmth of his body pressed against her back... She gets to hear his praise... She gets his hands running through her hair. Why is a beast allowed such intimate physical contact with Lord Sy, while I am forced to walk in the mud? I should be the one carrying him.’
Aeliana briefly entertained the fantasy of offering her own back for Silas to ride, but she quickly dismissed it.
Her physical strength wasn’t high enough to carry a fully armored Lord. She would just collapse and embarrass herself.

’I will simply have to endure this indignity...’ Aeliana concluded bitterly, shooting another toxic glare at the oblivious wolf. ’But if that animal drops him in the mud, I am turning it into a rug for his office.’
The banter carried them all the way to the edge of the ironwood forest.
The trees broke, revealing the massive towering black steel-weave walls of the Blessed Land looming in the damp twilight.
As they stepped out of the treeline and approached the closed iron gates, the wolf pack suddenly slowed down.
The Alpha male stopped completely, his ears pinning back against his skull. The females huddled together, letting out low nervous whines, while the pups darted behind their mother’s legs.
They were wild animals.
The scale of the towering steel walls terrified them.
Worse, their hyper-sensitive noses were suddenly assaulted by the overwhelming concentrated scent of dozens of human women, burning coal from the forge, and the sharp tang of metal weapons.
Silas’s mount shifted nervously beneath him with her paws digging into the mud as she hesitated to step any closer to the fortress.
"Easy," Silas murmured, leaning forward and resting his chest against her neck.
He stroked her fur, projecting his calm aura to counter her rising panic. "You’re safe. Nobody in there is going to hurt you."
Reina stepped forward, walking right up to the Alpha male. She didn’t use words this time.
She just placed her hand gently on the Alpha’s broad snout, letting her Beast Tamer resonance flow into his mind, reinforcing the protective promise Silas had made.
The Alpha let out a long shaky breath.
He looked at Silas, who was waiting patiently and then took a brave definitive step forward out of the mud and onto the clean black tiles of the outer perimeter.
"Open the gates!" Silas yelled up to the watchtowers.
The heavy gears ground loudly. The massive steel-weave portcullis slowly dragged upward, opening the path into the courtyard.
Silas nudged his mount’s sides with his knees.
The female wolf took a breath and trotted forward, leading the pack straight through the gates and into the Blessed Land.
The timing couldn’t have been more dramatic.
The afternoon training drills had just concluded.

Dozens of armored infantry girls, archers, and shieldmaidens were milling about the massive central courtyard, carrying their practice weapons back to the armory racks or heading toward the mess hall for dinner.
When the gates opened, the entire base stopped what they were doing.
The loud chaotic noise of the courtyard died instantly.
Dozens of women stared in utter shock at the sight rolling through the main entrance.
They expected their Lord to return from the swamp covered in mud, carrying monster pelts or dragging a bag of raw ore.
Instead, Silas Graves rode into the courtyard sitting tall and proud on the back of a massive shimmering golden direwolf.
The beast was gorgeous, its fur glowing like captured sunlight against the dark slate tiles of the base.
Behind him, an entire pack of identically golden, majestic apex predators trotted obediently in formation, flanked by Commander Brida and the junior squad.
He looked like a mythic conqueror stepping out of an ancient legend.
"By the Goddess," a spear-fighter whispered, dropping her wooden weapon onto the tiles with a clatter.
"He actually brought back cavalry mounts," another girl gasped, her eyes wide. "They look like actual light magic!"
Silas didn’t ignore the awe of his troops.
He knew how important morale was.
He sat up straight, a confident, easy smirk on his face, and casually raised his right hand, offering the stunned recruits a relaxed, two-finger wave as he rode past them.
The courtyard erupted.
The girls cheered wildly, banging their wooden spears against their shields and whistling loudly.
The prospect of no longer having to march through the swamp on foot sent a wave of electric excitement through the ranks.
"Look at the babies!" one of the archers squealed as the three tiny golden pups trotted bravely behind the Alpha, their little tails wagging as they took in the sights of their new home.
Silas guided his mount through the crowd, heading straight across the eastern tiles toward the newly constructed Tier 3 Mythic Pack-Lord’s Sanctuary.
As they approached the massive, obsidian-walled Beast Pavilion, the wolves’ nervousness vanished completely.
The building’s integrated magical runes were working flawlessly.
The [Nature’s Calm] passive effect projected a soothing deep-forest resonance across the paddock that instantly washed away the anxiety of the new environment.
Silas pulled back gently on the wolf’s fur, bringing her to a halt just outside the Deep-Earth alloy gates of the enclosure.
He swung his leg over her back and dropped lightly onto the stone tiles and he gave her neck one last affectionate scratch before turning to Reina.
"Alright, Reina... they’re yours," Silas told her, stepping aside. "Get them settled in."
Reina didn’t hesitate.
She stepped up to the heavy gates and threw the iron latch, pulling the doors wide open.
"Come on," Reina clicked her tongue, gesturing for the Alpha to follow her.
The golden pack trotted into the spacious open-air training paddock and the transformation in their demeanor was instant.
The moment their wide paws touched the thermal-heated stone tiles of the floor, the tension bled entirely out of their muscles.
The younger brother wolf, who had been shivering slightly from the cold, immediately dropped onto his belly on the warm stone, letting out a long dramatic groan of pure comfort.
