chapters.title: Chapter 145: Dressing Montage At Weaver’s Spire!
paragraphs: The cracked asphalt turned into smooth swept cobblestones.

The garish blinding neon billboards advertising mercenary contracts and cheap health potions vanished, replaced entirely by elegant glowing starlight lamps and manicured, enchanted flora lining the sidewalks.
The air outside the taxi stopped smelling like regular and it changed into the crisp clean scent of imported pine and purified ambient mana.
"We’re here, sir," the driver announced, pulling the taxi to a smooth halt along a pristine curb. "The Silverleaf Commercial District."
Silas nudged Lia gently. "Wake up. We’re here."
Lia groaned, sitting up and rubbing the sleep out of her eyes.
Silas opened the door, stepping out onto the cobblestones and turning back to the partition.
"Wait right here," Silas instructed the driver, pointing a firm finger at the man. "I’ll pay you triple your daily rate to take us back to my apartment when we’re done."
The driver’s eyes went wide with pure, unadulterated financial joy. "I won’t move an inch, my Lord! Take all the time you need!"
Silas closed the door and turned around.
Lia stepped out of the cab right behind him, completely freezing in place as she looked around.
The Silverleaf commercial district was overwhelming... It was where he stayed though he stayed in the residential one.
Massive multi-story buildings constructed almost entirely from enchanted reinforced glass and pristine white marble towered over them.
The display windows were filled with incredibly intricate, glowing silk garments, tailored coats, and mannequins draped in high-end tactical wear that cost more than a slum block’s annual GDP.
Standing directly in front of them was the sprawling, immaculate boutique.
The gold-leaf sign above the double doors practically glowed in the night air: [The Weaver’s Spire].
"Silas..." Lia whispered, her jaw hanging open as she stared at the glowing marble pillars. "This place looks like a palace. Are you sure they even let normal people in here?"
"I’m not a normal person anymore," Silas stated flatly.
He placed his hand on the small of her back and pushed her forward. "Walk."
They approached the heavy glass double doors. They slid open silently, powered by proximity runes.
The exact moment Silas and Lia stepped inside, they were assaulted by an overwhelming change.
The interior of Weaver’s Spire didn’t smell like the damp city rain.
It smelled aggressively of imported lavender expensive floral perfumes, and the crisp, undeniable scent of freshly pressed enchanted linen.

The lighting was soft and incredibly warm, designed to highlight the flawless stitching of the garments on display. Soft classical string music played from hidden magical acoustic crystals embedded in the high ceiling.

The boutique was busier than the last time Silas had been here... There were several actual customers... wealthy aristocratic women and high-tier corporate wives browsing the silk scarf racks and inspecting the outerwear.
Thankfully, there was no arrogant, screaming Young Master in sight.
Standing behind the massive, polished white marble counter near the center of the showroom were the three female clerks dressed in their immaculate, perfectly tailored black-and-gold uniforms.
The lead clerk, a stunning woman with perfectly styled blonde hair, was currently ringing up a purchase for an older woman draped in furs.

Silas walked directly toward the counter, his heavy boots clicking rhythmically against the pristine hardwood floor. Lia trailed nervously behind him, hyper-aware of the dirty puddles her worn sneakers were leaving on the immaculate floorboards.
As Silas approached, the blonde clerk looked up.
Her professional rehearsed customer-service smile instantly vanished, replaced by an expression of complete shock.
She recognized him immediately.

It was impossible to forget the ridiculously handsome, terrifyingly broad-shouldered Lord who had literally backhanded a Blackwood noble across the room, ordered two hundred and sixteen custom outfits, and casually dropped four hundred thousand Spirit Credits without blinking...
"L-Lord Graves!" Elise gasped, completely abandoning the older woman in furs to practically throw herself over the marble counter in greeting.
Her cheeks instantly flushed a brilliant violently hot shade of crimson. "Welcome back to Weaver’s Spire! It is an absolute honor to see you again so soon!"
The other two clerks looked up, their eyes widening in identical terrified infatuation as they simultaneously bowed deeply behind the register.
Silas stopped at the counter. He offered Elise a simple, polite nod.
"Good evening, Elise."
Elise looked like she was about to faint from the validation of him remembering her name.

"How may I serve you today, my Lord? Do you require further adjustments to the order for your soldiers? We already have fifty of the reinforced combat tunics running through the runic looms as we speak!"
"The other ones you gave me are fine," Silas replied smoothly, waving off the concern.
He stepped to the side, reaching out and gently pulling Lia out from behind his heavy trench coat.
Elise blinked, looking down at the small incredibly scruffy eleven-year-old girl drowning in the oversized gray t-shirt.
"This is my sister, Lia," Silas introduced her, his deep voice carrying authority.
He looked directly into Elise’s eyes. "I want you to customize her... Make her look quite pretty, and give her the highest quality, most durable clothes you have in your inventory. I’m paying."
Elise’s entire professional demeanor changed in a fraction of a second.
She didn’t look at Lia with the disgust an aristocrat usually reserved for a slum-rat. She looked at Lia like she was staring at a blank lucrative canvas handed to her by a god of wealth.
"It would be my pleasure, Lord Graves," Elise breathed out, her eyes shining with predatory tailoring instincts.
"Wait, what?" Lia panicked, her eyes darting between Silas and the blonde clerk. "No, wait, I just need a sweater! Seriously, I’m fine with just a—"
"Take her," Silas ordered.
"Girls!" Elise snapped her fingers, her voice cutting across the boutique ruthlessly.
The other two clerks moved with terrifying precision.
They flanked Lia instantly, grabbing the eleven-year-old girl firmly by the arms before she could even process what was happening.
"Let me go!" Lia shrieked, kicking her worn-out sneakers wildly against the floorboards as they physically hoisted her off the ground. "Silas! Help me! They’re kidnapping me! It’s a trap!"

"We promise to take excellent care of her, my Lord," Elise assured him with a bright terrifying smile, completely ignoring the screaming child as she grabbed a glowing digital measuring tape off the counter. "Please, have a seat. We will show you the options as we build the wardrobe."
"Have fun," Silas called out dryly, walking over to a plush high-backed velvet chair positioned directly outside the heavy oak doors of the primary fitting rooms.
He sat down, crossing his long legs and resting his arms on the armrests.
For the next forty-five minutes, Weaver’s Spire descended into a chaotic expensive fashion montage that was now usual anytime Silas was around.
The heavy oak door to the fitting room swung open.
Lia trudged out, her arms crossed aggressively over her chest with her face burning bright red.
Elise had dressed her in a ridiculously frilly, layered noble gown made of pale pink silk, complete with highly impractical, stiff leather dress shoes and a massive bow tied around her waist.
Lia looked like a deeply unhappy, highly explosive cupcake.
"Absolutely not..." Silas rejected it instantly, shaking his head. "She can’t run in that. If a low-tier slime jumped out of an alley, that skirt would trip her before she could draw a knife."
"I am not wearing this!" Lia yelled, glaring at him. "Do you know how much this costs?! The tag says two thousand credits! For a bow! Take it off me!"
’I mean it’s quite cheap though...’ Silas thought.
Elise materialized behind her, completely unbothered by the rejection. "Understood, my Lord! High mobility. We will adjust!"
Elise grabbed Lia by the shoulders and dragged her backward into the fitting room.
Ten minutes later, the door swung open again.
This time, Lia walked out looking entirely different.

Elise had dressed her in a sleek, high-end urban stealth outfit. She wore a pair of dark, reinforced denim pants, a fitted breathable black shirt, and a stunning, deep-crimson jacket woven from temperature-regulating spider-silk.
Her ratty sneakers were gone, replaced by a pair of sturdy polished black leather boots with silent anti-slip soles.
Lia looked down at her hands, flexing her fingers.
The clothes fit her perfectly, hugging her small frame without restricting her movement.
She looked like her big Brother though she would never be as cool as him.
"Now that," Silas noted, leaning forward in his velvet chair and resting his chin on his knuckles, "is much better."
He looked critically at the stitching.

"The material on the jacket is good. Spider-silk handles kinetic friction well. But check the gussets around the knees on the denim. If she has to drop into a crouch or climb a fire escape for example, standard denim will chafe. Reinforce the inner lining with a soft, breathable mana-weave."
Elise practically swooned at his deep evaluation. "Your eye for detail is simply magnificent, Lord Graves! I will have the seamstresses reinforce the joints immediately!"

"This jacket feels weird," Lia muttered, though she couldn’t hide the small amazed smile touching the corners of her lips as she zipped it up. "It’s super light, but I’m completely warm. It’s like wearing a heater."
"It’s enchanted," Silas told her flatly.

He looked at Elise. "I want five sets of the pants, ten of the breathable shirts in different dark colors, and three of those spider-silk jackets... Red, dark blue, and black. Make sure the boots are treated for heavy water resistance."
Lia’s eyes widened in horror. She grabbed the price tag dangling from the sleeve of the jacket and violently flipped it over.
"Five sets?!" Lia shrieked, her voice cracking. "Silas! This jacket alone is four thousand credits! You are literally buying enough clothes to fund a rebel army! Stop it!"

"Throw in three sets of heavy winter sleepwear and a durable duffel bag to carry it all in..." Silas instructed Elise, completely ignoring the screaming eleven-year-old. "And a pair of comfortable running shoes."
"Yes, my Lord!" Elise beamed, furiously typing the massive order into her glowing datapad. "We will have it packed and magically compressed into the duffel bag within ten minutes!"
Elise dragged Lia back into the fitting room to change her back into the newly purchased tactical gear so she could walk out wearing it.
Silas leaned back in his plush velvet chair, letting out a long satisfied exhale.
Dressing his sister in high-end wear wasn’t just a flex of his new wealth... it was a baseline security measure.

If he was going to be dragging her around Valoria City or hiding her in his apartment while he ran his territory, she needed clothing that could absorb a minor magical impact and boots that would let her run away if things went sideways.
He reached into the inner pocket of his trench coat and pulled out his phone to check the time.
The exact second the screen lit up, Silas froze.
The phone didn’t show the standard lock screen.
It was flashing with a massive, blaring red priority notification that overrode all of his internal system apps.
The notification banner carried the distinct encrypted golden seal of the Country’s High Council... the pinnacle of authority within the terrestrial World Government.
Silas tapped the notification.
The screen expanded into a breaking news bulletin broadcast across every registered Lord terminal in the region.
[BREAKING NEWS: THE SPONSORSHIP OFFER FROM THE WORD COUNCIL TO THE LORD OF BLESSED LAND HAS GONE UP FROM 3 BILLION TO EIGHT BILLION!]

[The Valoria High Council recognizes the unprecedented regional score achieved by the independent territory designated as ’Blessed Land’. The World Government is formally offering an immediate uncontested 8 Billion SC buyout for the complete transfer of territorial rights, blueprints, and authority. Any Lord with verifiable proof of ownership is commanded to report to the Central Spire immediately.]
Silas stared at the glowing screen as the numbers completely flatlined his brain.
’Eight billion,’ Silas thought with a cold chill spreading through his veins. ’Eight... billion. That isn’t just money... That is the GDP of a small country!’
He didn’t feel a rush of excitement nor did he feel the euphoric high of hitting the ultimate jackpot.
He felt a massive, suffocating target being painted directly onto his back.
Silas let out a heavy, tired sigh, slumping lower in the velvet chair.
"I’m not selling my rights..."
He muttered the words aloud.
He didn’t mind negotiating. In fact, his inner cynic loved the idea of scamming the World Government.

He could easily walk into the Central Spire, demand a massive upfront advance, sign a bunch of legally ambiguous proxy contracts, and leverage his combat superiority to gut the world government dry without giving them a single square inch of his actual territory.
But there was a massive critical flaw in that plan...
He needed a disguise.

sentences.text: The cracked asphalt turned into smooth swept cobblestones.

The garish blinding neon billboards advertising mercenary contracts and cheap health potions vanished, replaced entirely by elegant glowing starlight lamps and manicured, enchanted flora lining the sidewalks.
The air outside the taxi stopped smelling like regular and it changed into the crisp clean scent of imported pine and purified ambient mana.
"We’re here, sir," the driver announced, pulling the taxi to a smooth halt along a pristine curb.
"The Silverleaf Commercial District."
Silas nudged Lia gently.
"Wake up.
We’re here."
Lia groaned, sitting up and rubbing the sleep out of her eyes.
Silas opened the door, stepping out onto the cobblestones and turning back to the partition.
"Wait right here," Silas instructed the driver, pointing a firm finger at the man.
"I’ll pay you triple your daily rate to take us back to my apartment when we’re done."
The driver’s eyes went wide with pure, unadulterated financial joy.
"I won’t move an inch, my Lord!
Take all the time you need!"
Silas closed the door and turned around.
Lia stepped out of the cab right behind him, completely freezing in place as she looked around.
The Silverleaf commercial district was overwhelming...
It was where he stayed though he stayed in the residential one.
Massive multi-story buildings constructed almost entirely from enchanted reinforced glass and pristine white marble towered over them.
The display windows were filled with incredibly intricate, glowing silk garments, tailored coats, and mannequins draped in high-end tactical wear that cost more than a slum block’s annual GDP.
Standing directly in front of them was the sprawling, immaculate boutique.
The gold-leaf sign above the double doors practically glowed in the night air: [The Weaver’s Spire].
"Silas..." Lia whispered, her jaw hanging open as she stared at the glowing marble pillars.
"This place looks like a palace.
Are you sure they even let normal people in here?"
"I’m not a normal person anymore," Silas stated flatly.
He placed his hand on the small of her back and pushed her forward.
"Walk."
They approached the heavy glass double doors.
They slid open silently, powered by proximity runes.
The exact moment Silas and Lia stepped inside, they were assaulted by an overwhelming change.
The interior of Weaver’s Spire didn’t smell like the damp city rain.
It smelled aggressively of imported lavender expensive floral perfumes, and the crisp, undeniable scent of freshly pressed enchanted linen.
The lighting was soft and incredibly warm, designed to highlight the flawless stitching of the garments on display.
Soft classical string music played from hidden magical acoustic crystals embedded in the high ceiling.
The boutique was busier than the last time Silas had been here...
There were several actual customers... wealthy aristocratic women and high-tier corporate wives browsing the silk scarf racks and inspecting the outerwear.
Thankfully, there was no arrogant, screaming Young Master in sight.
Standing behind the massive, polished white marble counter near the center of the showroom were the three female clerks dressed in their immaculate, perfectly tailored black-and-gold uniforms.
The lead clerk, a stunning woman with perfectly styled blonde hair, was currently ringing up a purchase for an older woman draped in furs.
Silas walked directly toward the counter, his heavy boots clicking rhythmically against the pristine hardwood floor.
Lia trailed nervously behind him, hyper-aware of the dirty puddles her worn sneakers were leaving on the immaculate floorboards.
As Silas approached, the blonde clerk looked up.
Her professional rehearsed customer-service smile instantly vanished, replaced by an expression of complete shock.
She recognized him immediately.

It was impossible to forget the ridiculously handsome, terrifyingly broad-shouldered Lord who had literally backhanded a Blackwood noble across the room, ordered two hundred and sixteen custom outfits, and casually dropped four hundred thousand Spirit Credits without blinking...
"L-Lord Graves!" Elise gasped, completely abandoning the older woman in furs to practically throw herself over the marble counter in greeting.
Her cheeks instantly flushed a brilliant violently hot shade of crimson.
"Welcome back to Weaver’s Spire!
It is an absolute honor to see you again so soon!"
The other two clerks looked up, their eyes widening in identical terrified infatuation as they simultaneously bowed deeply behind the register.
Silas stopped at the counter.
He offered Elise a simple, polite nod.
"Good evening, Elise."
Elise looked like she was about to faint from the validation of him remembering her name.
"How may I serve you today, my Lord?
Do you require further adjustments to the order for your soldiers?
We already have fifty of the reinforced combat tunics running through the runic looms as we speak!"
"The other ones you gave me are fine," Silas replied smoothly, waving off the concern.
He stepped to the side, reaching out and gently pulling Lia out from behind his heavy trench coat.
Elise blinked, looking down at the small incredibly scruffy eleven-year-old girl drowning in the oversized gray t-shirt.
"This is my sister, Lia," Silas introduced her, his deep voice carrying authority.
He looked directly into Elise’s eyes.
"I want you to customize her...
Make her look quite pretty, and give her the highest quality, most durable clothes you have in your inventory.
I’m paying."
Elise’s entire professional demeanor changed in a fraction of a second.
She didn’t look at Lia with the disgust an aristocrat usually reserved for a slum-rat.
She looked at Lia like she was staring at a blank lucrative canvas handed to her by a god of wealth.
"It would be my pleasure, Lord Graves," Elise breathed out, her eyes shining with predatory tailoring instincts.
"Wait, what?" Lia panicked, her eyes darting between Silas and the blonde clerk.
"No, wait, I just need a sweater!
Seriously, I’m fine with just a—"
"Take her," Silas ordered.
"Girls!" Elise snapped her fingers, her voice cutting across the boutique ruthlessly.
The other two clerks moved with terrifying precision.
They flanked Lia instantly, grabbing the eleven-year-old girl firmly by the arms before she could even process what was happening.
"Let me go!" Lia shrieked, kicking her worn-out sneakers wildly against the floorboards as they physically hoisted her off the ground.
"Silas!
Help me!
They’re kidnapping me!
It’s a trap!"

"We promise to take excellent care of her, my Lord," Elise assured him with a bright terrifying smile, completely ignoring the screaming child as she grabbed a glowing digital measuring tape off the counter.
"Please, have a seat.
We will show you the options as we build the wardrobe."
"Have fun," Silas called out dryly, walking over to a plush high-backed velvet chair positioned directly outside the heavy oak doors of the primary fitting rooms.
He sat down, crossing his long legs and resting his arms on the armrests.
For the next forty-five minutes, Weaver’s Spire descended into a chaotic expensive fashion montage that was now usual anytime Silas was around.
The heavy oak door to the fitting room swung open.
Lia trudged out, her arms crossed aggressively over her chest with her face burning bright red.
Elise had dressed her in a ridiculously frilly, layered noble gown made of pale pink silk, complete with highly impractical, stiff leather dress shoes and a massive bow tied around her waist.
Lia looked like a deeply unhappy, highly explosive cupcake.

For a bow!
Take it off me!"

High mobility.
We will adjust!"

Elise had dressed her in a sleek, high-end urban stealth outfit.

chapters.title: Chapter 146: News
paragraphs: ’If I had nothing to lose...’ Silas thought coldly with his blue eyes narrowing at the glowing screen. ’If it was just me, I would use my real name. I would walk into the High Council, take their money, and if they tried to screw me, I would drop Morwenna and Eluned into their lobby and let them burn the building to the ground...’
He slowly looked up from his phone, staring at the closed oak door of the fitting room.
’But I have Lia now and not only that, I have to be very careful...’ Silas realized.
If he exposed his true identity as the Warlord of the Blessed Land to the World Government, he wouldn’t just be risking his own neck.
The major corporate guilds were absolutely ruthless. They didn’t fight fair. If they couldn’t control him through contracts, they would look for leverage.
They would find out about his eleven-year-old sister living in his apartment.
They would send an elite strike team of assassins to kidnap her while he was offline, and they would hold her hostage until he signed over the deeds to the territory.
There was also the possibility of them tracing down where Blessed Land was in the Sovereign Realm and raid it as Lords, killing him and taking control of his people.

’I can’t bring her into the Sovereign Realm.... And I need to be stronger to protect not only her but myself and my women.’ Silas thought with a deep frustration burning in his chest. ’Only awakened Lords and registered summoners can cross the planar threshold... A baseline human child would be atomized by the transit pressure, or instantly poisoned by the ambient miasma in the Sovereign Realm, and that’s without mentioning the Umbral Basin so she has to stay on Earth.’
He rubbed his temples.
He needed to build an entirely fake identity.
He needed a proxy Lord, a mask, or some kind of impenetrable corporate shell company to interact with the High Council so the name Silas Graves remained completely unconnected to the Blessed Land.
Before he could fully map out the logistics of creating a fake corporate entity, his phone buzzed violently in his hand.
The blaring red High Council notification vanished, replaced by a direct, highly encrypted ping from Elora Verinda.
Silas swiped the message open.
[Elora: I see the High Council just put an eight billion credit reward on the Blessed Land. The entire city is going crazy. But that’s a problem for later.]
[Elora: Oh right, I forgot to tell you about a specific parameter for this Secret Realm expedition tonight.]
Silas frowned with his eyes scanning the text.
[Elora: Because it is a volatile spatial fracture, the entry is severely restricted to prevent a mana collapse. You cannot bring your entire squad....]
Silas felt a sharp spike of annoyance.
He had fully planned to bring Morwenna, Eluned, and Aeliana to completely steamroll whatever ancient boss monster was guarding the vault.
He read the final line of the text message and his eyes went completely wide.
[Elora: To this Secret Realm expedition, you may only bring one of your Summons... whether it be your Hero or Troop.]
Silas blinked, staring at the glowing screen of his phone.
The rhythmic bass of the boutique’s classical string music played softly in the background, but his brain had completely stalled out in the plush velvet chair.
He stared at the final text message Elora had just sent him.
[Elora: To this Secret Realm expedition, you may only bring one of your Summons... whether it be your Hero or Troop.]
Silas didn’t hesitate. His thumbs flew across the digital keyboard.
[Silas: What?]
He watched the screen.
At the bottom of the encrypted chat window, three small gray dots appeared, pulsing in a wave to indicate that Elora was actively typing her response.
The dots vanished and a new text bubble popped up.

[Elora: Like I said, the mana of the spatial fracture is quite volatile. If we flood the entrance with too many high-density entities at once, the portal will destabilize and collapse the ruin... The absolute capacity the threshold can handle without triggering a spatial cave-in is already hit if everyone brings one of their Troops or Heroes. I am bringing one of my elite elemental guards and you are allowed to bring at least one person with you which is why you have to think very carefully about the person you are bringing to the expedition.]
Silas leaned his head back against the velvet chair, letting out a long, heavy sigh. He stared at the ceiling of the Weaver’s Spire.
’So much for steamrolling the boss with an army...’ Silas thought bitterly.
He tapped the screen.
[Silas: Oh... I see...]
He watched the chat interface, expecting her to send a location ping or a time for the raid so he could start prepping his gear.
The three gray typing dots appeared again. They pulsed for a few seconds.
[Elora: That’s fine, now about the date...]
Silas’s golden-ringed eyes went completely wide. He physically jolted in the velvet chair, staring at the word ’date’.
’I thought she was joking before...’
Before he could even process the sentence, the message bubble instantly vanished from the screen. It was deleted so fast it was almost as if it had never been there.
A split second later, a new brief message replaced it.
[Elora: Ok.]
Silas lowered the phone slowly, letting it rest on his knee. He stared blankly across the aisle of the boutique, completely ignoring the mannequins draped in expensive silk.
’What the hell?’ Silas thought. ’I don’t think I’m so handsome that the School Belle would be this anxious to want to go on a date with me.’
Elora Verinda was the City Lord’s daughter.

She was cold and ran her faction like a corporate CEO... She didn’t make typos, and she certainly didn’t accidentally invite slum-born independents on romantic outings while negotiating high-tier mercenary raids.

’Unless she’s trying to honey-trap me to secure the Secret Realm loot,’ Silas analyzed coldly. ’She knows I have physical strength and she might be trying to play an angle. Or... her auto-correct just completely botched whatever sentence she was actually trying to type.’
He pushed the bizarre text message to the back of his mind. He didn’t have time to decipher the romantic intentions of a noble teenager but... the major thing was quite different.
The restriction of the Secret Realm raid had completely flipped his tactical approach on its head.
If he was only bringing one of his people to the raid, he needed to think carefully.
Silas crossed his arms over his chest, his eyes narrowing as he ran through his Vanguard roster.

’I can’t bring Eluned... Just bringing Morwenna or Eluned will cause a lot of trouble.’ Silas thought instantly, he had been joking when he had thought he would include those two. ’She is the Goddess of Nature... Her aura literally causes grass to grow out of the floorboards wherever she walks as long as she wills it. If I walk into a Secret Realm with a mythic-tier divine entity trailing behind me, Elora will instantly realize I’m not a baseline Blue Core. She’ll put two and two together, and my identity as the Lord of Blessed Land gets exposed to the High Council.’
He shifted his weight in the velvet chair.
’Neither could I bring Morwenna either,’ Silas concluded.
The Dread Queen of the Astral Seas was an SSS-rank powerhouse, but subtlety was not in her vocabulary.
She carried a massive anchor and solved ninety percent of her problems by throwing her enemies through walls or outright killing them.
She was a divine-level brute force anomaly. There were no two ways about it; bringing either of them would be revealed instantly that he was the Lord of Blessed Land...
Going downward through the roster... he could bring Brida.
The heavy shieldmaiden was a physical juggernaut, completely capable of tanking boss-level hits.

He could bring Tasmin. The Huntress was a lethal, high-speed striker who could navigate a dark ruin flawlessly. He could even bring Vala or Elara for baseline scouting utility but he had to think about it. He had to talk to the girls about it as well to decide.
’However, from a purely tactical standpoint,’ Silas thought, rubbing his chin. ’Personally, Aeliana or Rowenna would fit the bill.’
Silas was a physical warrior.
He wielded a forty-pound mythril-laced broadsword, wore heavy armor, and relied on explosive close-quarters violence to butcher his enemies.
If Elora’s scouts were right and the boss monster guarding the vault was heavily armored, throwing more physical damage at it wasn’t the most efficient strategy.
He needed elemental suppression so in short, he needed crowd control.
’Mages wouldn’t be bad at all,’ Silas noted.
Aeliana was an Arcanist but Rowena... Rowena was the Runic Arcanist. They were both the same but different.

She was a dedicated Mage. If an ancient, heavily armored boss monster charged them in the dark, Rowena could drop a Tier 2 ten-times gravity well on the floor, pin the beast to the stone, and let Silas casually execute it.
Well, he would talk about that when he got home and went back to the girls. He locked his phone and slipped it into his inner coat pocket.
Right on cue, the heavy velvet curtain of the primary fitting room slid open.
Lia came out for the last time.
She wasn’t wearing the aggressive dark spider-silk gear Elise had tailored for her earlier.
That was packed away for whenever they needed to move through the city or run from corporate guild enforcers...
This time, Lia was wearing quite a beautiful dress that she could comfortably wear at home.
It was a simple, knee-length dress woven from incredibly soft, high-grade white cotton, completely free of the stiff restrictive corsets or gaudy bows that the noble children usually wore.
It had long, loose sleeves that gathered neatly at the wrists, a modest neckline, and a subtle dark blue ribbon tied loosely around the waist.
She wore a pair of clean, soft wool leggings underneath and simple, comfortable leather flats.
She didn’t look like a heavily armed street rat, and she didn’t look like a porcelain doll. She just looked like a normal incredibly well-cared-for eleven-year-old girl.

Lia stepped out onto the pristine hardwood floor, looking down at the hem of the white dress. She twirled slightly with the soft fabric flaring out around her knees as a small innocent smile broke across her face.
She looked up at Silas, nervously shifting her weight.
"I like it," Silas said immediately.
Lia’s smile widened, her dark eyes shining with happiness.
Elise, standing right behind her with a glowing datapad, practically melted at the domestic interaction.
They thanked him, took her back behind the velvet curtain, and made her pull it off so it could be folded, pressed, and properly packed away with the rest of her massive haul.
A few minutes later, Silas was standing at the polished white marble counter.
Lia stood right next to him.
She was back in the oversized dark gray t-shirt he had given her, though she had managed to roll the sleeves up enough to free her hands.
She was bouncing slightly on her worn-out sneakers, buzzing with the leftover adrenaline of trying on more expensive clothes in one hour than she had seen in her entire life.
Elise stood behind the counter, rapidly tallying the final additions to the massive order.

"Alright, Lord Graves," Elise smiled professionally, her fingers tapping the glowing runic terminal. "For the five sets of denim, the ten breathable combat shirts, the three enchanted spider-silk jackets, the heavy winter sleepwear, the water-resistant boots, the white cotton home dress, and the magically compressed duffel bag to carry it all..."
Elise paused, ensuring the total was correct.
They called the price.
"The final total comes to exactly 200,000 Spirit Credits," Elise announced clearly.
Lia went completely rigid.
The bouncing instantly stopped. The color drained out of her face so fast she looked like a ghost. Her jaw dropped open, her brown eyes bugging out of her skull as she stared at the glowing terminal.
Two hundred thousand?!
Lia’s street-rat brain short-circuited... She literally went into a seizure.
She grabbed the fabric of Silas’s trench coat with both hands, violently shaking his arm as she hyperventilated.

"Big Brother!" Lia gasped, her voice completely failing as she stared at the blonde clerk in horror. "Two hundred thousand?! For shirts?! Are they woven out of solid gold?! Cancel it! Cancel it right now! We can go to the thrift market! I don’t need the jackets! I don’t need the dress! Big Brother, I’m going to be homeless again!"

He had fully planned to bring Morwenna, Eluned, and Aeliana to completely steamroll whatever ancient boss monster was guarding the vault.
He read the final line of the text message and his eyes went completely wide.
[Elora: To this Secret Realm expedition, you may only bring one of your Summons... whether it be your Hero or Troop.]
Silas blinked, staring at the glowing screen of his phone.
The rhythmic bass of the boutique’s classical string music played softly in the background, but his brain had completely stalled out in the plush velvet chair.
He stared at the final text message Elora had just sent him.
[Elora: To this Secret Realm expedition, you may only bring one of your Summons... whether it be your Hero or Troop.]
Silas didn’t hesitate.
His thumbs flew across the digital keyboard.
[Silas: What?]
He watched the screen.
At the bottom of the encrypted chat window, three small gray dots appeared, pulsing in a wave to indicate that Elora was actively typing her response.
The dots vanished and a new text bubble popped up.
[Elora: Like I said, the mana of the spatial fracture is quite volatile.
If we flood the entrance with too many high-density entities at once, the portal will destabilize and collapse the ruin...
The absolute capacity the threshold can handle without triggering a spatial cave-in is already hit if everyone brings one of their Troops or Heroes.

I am bringing one of my elite elemental guards and you are allowed to bring at least one person with you which is why you have to think very carefully about the person you are bringing to the expedition.]
Silas leaned his head back against the velvet chair, letting out a long, heavy sigh.
He stared at the ceiling of the Weaver’s Spire.
’So much for steamrolling the boss with an army...’ Silas thought bitterly.
He tapped the screen.
[Silas: Oh...
I see...]
He watched the chat interface, expecting her to send a location ping or a time for the raid so he could start prepping his gear.
The three gray typing dots appeared again.
They pulsed for a few seconds.
[Elora: That’s fine, now about the date...]
Silas’s golden-ringed eyes went completely wide.
He physically jolted in the velvet chair, staring at the word ’date’.
’I thought she was joking before...’
Before he could even process the sentence, the message bubble instantly vanished from the screen.
It was deleted so fast it was almost as if it had never been there.
A split second later, a new brief message replaced it.
[Elora: Ok.]
Silas lowered the phone slowly, letting it rest on his knee.
He stared blankly across the aisle of the boutique, completely ignoring the mannequins draped in expensive silk.
’What the hell?’ Silas thought. ’I don’t think I’m so handsome that the School Belle would be this anxious to want to go on a date with me.’
Elora Verinda was the City Lord’s daughter.
She was cold and ran her faction like a corporate CEO...
She didn’t make typos, and she certainly didn’t accidentally invite slum-born independents on romantic outings while negotiating high-tier mercenary raids.
’Unless she’s trying to honey-trap me to secure the Secret Realm loot,’ Silas analyzed coldly. ’She knows I have physical strength and she might be trying to play an angle.
Or... her auto-correct just completely botched whatever sentence she was actually trying to type.’
He pushed the bizarre text message to the back of his mind.
He didn’t have time to decipher the romantic intentions of a noble teenager but... the major thing was quite different.
The restriction of the Secret Realm raid had completely flipped his tactical approach on its head.
If he was only bringing one of his people to the raid, he needed to think carefully.
Silas crossed his arms over his chest, his eyes narrowing as he ran through his Vanguard roster.
’I can’t bring Eluned...
Just bringing Morwenna or Eluned will cause a lot of trouble.’ Silas thought instantly, he had been joking when he had thought he would include those two. ’She is the Goddess of Nature...
Her aura literally causes grass to grow out of the floorboards wherever she walks as long as she wills it.
If I walk into a Secret Realm with a mythic-tier divine entity trailing behind me, Elora will instantly realize I’m not a baseline Blue Core.
She’ll put two and two together, and my identity as the Lord of Blessed Land gets exposed to the High Council.’
He shifted his weight in the velvet chair.
’Neither could I bring Morwenna either,’ Silas concluded.
The Dread Queen of the Astral Seas was an SSS-rank powerhouse, but subtlety was not in her vocabulary.
She carried a massive anchor and solved ninety percent of her problems by throwing her enemies through walls or outright killing them.
She was a divine-level brute force anomaly.
There were no two ways about it; bringing either of them would be revealed instantly that he was the Lord of Blessed Land...
Going downward through the roster... he could bring Brida.
The heavy shieldmaiden was a physical juggernaut, completely capable of tanking boss-level hits.
He could bring Tasmin.
The Huntress was a lethal, high-speed striker who could navigate a dark ruin flawlessly.
He could even bring Vala or Elara for baseline scouting utility but he had to think about it.
He had to talk to the girls about it as well to decide.
’However, from a purely tactical standpoint,’ Silas thought, rubbing his chin. ’Personally, Aeliana or Rowenna would fit the bill.’
Silas was a physical warrior.
He wielded a forty-pound mythril-laced broadsword, wore heavy armor, and relied on explosive close-quarters violence to butcher his enemies.
If Elora’s scouts were right and the boss monster guarding the vault was heavily armored, throwing more physical damage at it wasn’t the most efficient strategy.
He needed elemental suppression so in short, he needed crowd control.
’Mages wouldn’t be bad at all,’ Silas noted.
Aeliana was an Arcanist but Rowena...
Rowena was the Runic Arcanist.
They were both the same but different.
She was a dedicated Mage.
If an ancient, heavily armored boss monster charged them in the dark, Rowena could drop a Tier 2 ten-times gravity well on the floor, pin the beast to the stone, and let Silas casually execute it.
Well, he would talk about that when he got home and went back to the girls.
He locked his phone and slipped it into his inner coat pocket.
Right on cue, the heavy velvet curtain of the primary fitting room slid open.
Lia came out for the last time.
She wasn’t wearing the aggressive dark spider-silk gear Elise had tailored for her earlier.
That was packed away for whenever they needed to move through the city or run from corporate guild enforcers...
This time, Lia was wearing quite a beautiful dress that she could comfortably wear at home.
It was a simple, knee-length dress woven from incredibly soft, high-grade white cotton, completely free of the stiff restrictive corsets or gaudy bows that the noble children usually wore.
It had long, loose sleeves that gathered neatly at the wrists, a modest neckline, and a subtle dark blue ribbon tied loosely around the waist.
She wore a pair of clean, soft wool leggings underneath and simple, comfortable leather flats.
She didn’t look like a heavily armed street rat, and she didn’t look like a porcelain doll.
She just looked like a normal incredibly well-cared-for eleven-year-old girl.
Lia stepped out onto the pristine hardwood floor, looking down at the hem of the white dress.
She twirled slightly with the soft fabric flaring out around her knees as a small innocent smile broke across her face.
She looked up at Silas, nervously shifting her weight.
"I like it," Silas said immediately.
Lia’s smile widened, her dark eyes shining with happiness.
Elise, standing right behind her with a glowing datapad, practically melted at the domestic interaction.
They thanked him, took her back behind the velvet curtain, and made her pull it off so it could be folded, pressed, and properly packed away with the rest of her massive haul.
A few minutes later, Silas was standing at the polished white marble counter.
Lia stood right next to him.
She was back in the oversized dark gray t-shirt he had given her, though she had managed to roll the sleeves up enough to free her hands.
She was bouncing slightly on her worn-out sneakers, buzzing with the leftover adrenaline of trying on more expensive clothes in one hour than she had seen in her entire life.
Elise stood behind the counter, rapidly tallying the final additions to the massive order.
"Alright, Lord Graves," Elise smiled professionally, her fingers tapping the glowing runic terminal.

"For the five sets of denim, the ten breathable combat shirts, the three enchanted spider-silk jackets, the heavy winter sleepwear, the water-resistant boots, the white cotton home dress, and the magically compressed duffel bag to carry it all..."
Elise paused, ensuring the total was correct.
They called the price.
"The final total comes to exactly 200,000 Spirit Credits," Elise announced clearly.
Lia went completely rigid.
The bouncing instantly stopped.
The color drained out of her face so fast she looked like a ghost.
Her jaw dropped open, her brown eyes bugging out of her skull as she stared at the glowing terminal.
Two hundred thousand?!
Lia’s street-rat brain short-circuited...
She literally went into a seizure.
She grabbed the fabric of Silas’s trench coat with both hands, violently shaking his arm as she hyperventilated.
"Big Brother!" Lia gasped, her voice completely failing as she stared at the blonde clerk in horror.
"Two hundred thousand?!
For shirts?!
Are they woven out of solid gold?!
Cancel it!
Cancel it right now!
We can go to the thrift market!
I don’t need the jackets!
I don’t need the dress!
Big Brother, I’m going to be homeless again!"

chapters.title: Chapter 147: Sibling Time
paragraphs: Silas didn’t even flinch. He simply reached his calloused hand down and patted her messy hair, completely ignoring her financial meltdown.
"It’s fine... you just have to calm down." Silas told her calmly.
He pulled his phone from his pocket, leaned over the marble counter, and tapped the screen against the glowing scanner.
CHIME!
[Transaction Approved. 200,000 SC Deducted.]
Lia let out a pathetic high-pitched squeak of pure economic trauma, completely defeated by the reality that her brother had just spent two hundred thousand credits on her wardrobe without blinking.

Elise beamed, sliding a sleek dark canvas duffel bag across the marble counter. It looked no larger than a standard gym bag, but Silas knew the interior was laced with expansion runes to effortlessly hold the massive pile of clothing they had just purchased.
He grabbed the heavy strap of the bag.
He didn’t sling it over his shoulder. In a flash of golden pixelated light, he put it directly into his Lord Inventory, letting the bag vanish into the spatial void.
"Your business is always appreciated, Lord Graves," Elise bowed deeply, pressing her hand over her heart. "Please, do not hesitate to contact me if the young miss requires any further alterations."
Lia, still completely catatonic from the price tag, managed a weak polite bow. She thanked her quietly though her voice was barely above a whisper.

Silas gave the clerk a respectful nod. He wished goodbye to Elise and the rest of the boutique staff, who were all gathered near the back racks, watching the ridiculously wealthy and handsome Lord depart.
They all greeted him too, waving him off with flushed cheeks and eager smiles.

Silas placed his hand on the small of Lia’s back, guiding the shell-shocked eleven-year-old out of the warm lavender-scented air of the Weaver’s Spire and back out into the cool, damp night of the Valoria City commercial district.
The rain had started up again, a light freezing drizzle that slicked the cobblestones.
Silas didn’t have to wait.
The grizzled taxi driver he had bribed earlier was parked exactly where they had left him with the engine idling warmly by the curb.
Silas opened the back door. They went outside, stepped out of the rain, and entered the cab.
"Welcome back, my Lord!" the driver greeted them enthusiastically, clearly thrilled to be earning triple his daily rate. "Heading straight back to the Silverleaf residential sector?"

"Yeah," Silas said, pulling the door shut. He paused, looking out the rain-streaked window at the glowing neon storefronts lining the street. "Actually, make a stop first. Pull over at the nearest high-end convenience store on the way."
"You got it, boss," the driver nodded, throwing the cab into drive.
They drove for about five minutes down the primary commercial artery before the driver pulled up to a massive, brightly lit storefront.
The neon sign above the sliding glass doors read: [Ether-Mart: Premium Provisions].
Silas stepped out of the cab, pulling Lia along with him.
The little girl was still muttering quietly to herself about the two hundred thousand credits, completely lost in a traumatic trance of financial guilt.
"I told you not to worry, didn’t I?"
They walked through the sliding glass doors.
The convenience store was massive and impeccably clean too, it was also fully stocked with high-tier terrestrial goods.
This wasn’t the grimy flickering bodega in the slums that sold expired synthetic nutrient paste and stale cheese blocks.
This place catered to the corporate elite and the wealthy.
The aisles were lined with fresh organically grown produce, magically preserved cuts of premium terrestrial meat, and rows upon rows of brightly colored expensive snacks.
Silas grabbed a heavy wire shopping basket near the entrance.
"Alright," Silas said, handing the basket to Lia. "We’re buying food. Real food."
Lia snapped out of her trance. She looked down at the basket, then up at the towering shelves of food.
Her stomach, which had been surviving on cheap spaghetti and tap water for quite some time gave a loud treacherous rumble.
They walked down the first aisle.
Lia’s eyes widened.
She stared at the shelves with her t instincts immediately defaulting to her old habits.
She reached out tentatively and grabbed a small, crushed box of generic grain crackers, the cheapest item on the shelf as she carefully placed it into the wire basket.
’Sigh... would it kill thie girl to be a bit more stingy?’
Silas stopped walking.
He looked down at the crushed box of generic crackers and helooked at Lia.
Without a word, Silas reached into the basket, picked up the crushed box, and casually tossed it back onto the shelf.
"Hey!" Lia protested, her brow furrowing. "Those were only two credits!"
Silas ignored her.
He reached out and grabbed five massive brightly colored boxes of premium enchanted sugar cookies, a large bag of expensive salted root-chips, and three heavy jars of roasted honey-glazed nuts.
He dumped all of them unceremoniously into her wire basket.
"We aren’t eating garbage anymore, Lia." Silas told her flatly.
Lia stared at the mountain of expensive snacks weighing down the basket. "Silas... this is like... fifty credits worth of snacks."
"It’s alright," Silas reminded her, tapping the side of her head. "Keep walking."
They moved through the store like an invading army.
Silas bought stuff apart from spaghetti.
He completely bypassed the dry goods and walked directly to the refrigerated butcher section at the back of the store.
He didn’t buy ground beef or cheap sausage links.
He selected three massive thick-cut, premium marbled terrestrial ribeye steaks.
"Hehe~"
He grabbed fresh cloves of garlic, sprigs of real rosemary, heavy blocks of sharp aged white cheddar cheese, and a massive carton of fresh eggs.
’This is what I mean when I say good food...’
Lia followed him with her eyes growing wider and wider at every item he dumped into the basket.
By the time they reached the checkout counter, the wire basket was overflowing with premium groceries.
The cashier rang them up.
Silas tapped his phone against the scanner, paid the tab without checking the price, and grabbed the heavy paper grocery bags.
They went back outside, climbed back into the warm waiting taxi, and drove the rest of the way to the Silverleaf residential complex.
"Sigh... Night man."
Silas paid the driver the promised triple rate, earning a salute from the exhausted man and led Lia up the elevator to their apartment.
The Spirit lock chimed with the door swinging open to reveal the quiet dimly lit living room.
Silas didn’t drop the bags on the counter and order her to go to sleep.
He walked straight into the small modern kitchen, set the groceries down on the marble island, and began unpacking them.
"Wash your hands," Silas instructed, rolling up the sleeves of his dark formal shirt. "You’re helping me cook..."
Lia blinked, surprised.
She quickly dragged a stool over to the sink, climbed up, and scrubbed her hands with soap.
Lia then hopped down and trotted over to the island, peering into the bags.
"What are we making?" Lia asked, her mouth watering at the sight of the thick-cut ribeye steaks.
"Steak and eggs," Silas replied simply. "A proper meal and none of that cheap pasta you were boiling earlier."
For the next thirty minutes, the quiet apartment transformed.

Silas had wondered what he was going to use to fill this place up... he had bought a good apartment and it was almost like he had no use for it since he had no connection to Earth apart from the fact that the LAB was here but all of that had changed now.
They cooked together. Silas handled the heavy work, dropping a cast-iron skillet onto the gas burner and letting it heat up until it was smoking.
He seasoned the massive steaks heavily with coarse salt and cracked black pepper.
Lia stood on her stool next to him, assigned to the critical task of peeling and crushing the fresh garlic cloves.
Shh Shh Shh!
She smacked the cloves with the flat of a kitchen knife, laughing as the papery skins flew off onto the counter.
Silas on the other hand dropped the steaks into the blistering hot pan.
HISSSSS!
The loud violent sound of searing meat filled the kitchen as a thick rich cloud of sizzling fat, crushed garlic, and roasting rosemary plumed into the air.
Silas grabbed a spoon, tilted the pan slightly, and began rapidly basting the searing steaks with melting butter and garlic.
Lia watched him, completely mesmerized by the effortless skill he displayed.
"You cook like a professional, Big brother. You never cooked like this before when we were living together."

"I never had ribeye steaks in the slums," Silas chuckled with his eyes focused on the searing meat. "And I’ve had a lot of practice recently. My head chef in the territory is a perfectionist... and she does a lot of work. If I burn the meat, she looks like she’s going to cry and I watch her cook when I’m free."
Lia nodded, she didn’t understand most of these stuff but she did know her Big Brother was having an excellent time and honestly that was enough for her.
He pulled the perfectly seared medium-rare steaks out of the pan, resting them on a wooden cutting board to let the juices settle.
He cracked four fresh eggs directly into the residual garlic butter left in the cast iron, frying them up perfectly with crispy, golden edges.
The apartment smelled incredible.
Silas stood at the kitchen island, wiping his hands on a towel.
He was smiling.
It was a genuine relaxed smile at the aroma of the food filling his home here... It felt quite normal.
’Though I still want to head back to Blessed Land but it’s probably when she falls asleep.’ Silas thought.
They plated the food.
Silas transferred the massive cuts of steak onto two ceramic plates, sliding the perfectly fried eggs right on top, and carried them over to the small kitchen table.
They sat down across from each other.
Lia didn’t wait for permission.
She grabbed her fork and knife, sliced a piece of the steak, and shoved it into her mouth.
"Mmmh~"
Her eyes rolled into the back of her head and a soft groan of pure bliss escaped her lips as the rich garlic-infused fat melted on her tongue.
It was, without a single doubt, the greatest thing she had ever eaten in her entire ten years of life!
Silas cut into his own steak, chewing quietly as he watched her inhale her food like a starving wolf pup.
He took a sip of his water. He set the glass down, resting his forearms on the table.
Silas looked directly at his sister.
"So, Lia," Silas asked with his deep voice cutting smoothly through the quiet kitchen.
Lia paused, a piece of steak halfway to her mouth. She looked across the table at him as her dark eyes were wide and curious.
Silas rested his chin on his folded hands, his golden-ringed eyes locking onto hers.
"Are you still interested in heading to school?"
School.
It was something she had always wanted.

Ever since Silas had pulled her out of that freezing rotting dumpster in the lower wards, she had watched the clean, well-dressed children walk past the alleyways in their pristine uniforms, carrying heavy textbooks and glowing datapads.
They were learning about history, magic theory, and global economics, while she was learning how to pickpocket distracted tourists just to afford synthetic nutrient paste.
She had wanted to go so badly. And Silas was well aware of it.
Before she had run away, before the guilt of being a financial burden had driven her into the dark, Silas had a plan.

His original goal had been quite simple: he would finish his brutal, grinding curriculum at the Valoria Academy, graduate with a baseline placement, and use his entry-level salary to put her in a decent preparatory section fitting of her age.
He wanted her to learn.
He wanted her to understand the complex mechanics of the world in case she was lucky enough to awaken a core and become a Lord herself.

He banked on the fact that if he became a registered Lord... even a lowly Red Core, he would be granted priority placement for his dependents but then she stole his money and vanished, and the plan had died.
Until now...
Lia slowly lowered her fork with the heavy metal clinking against the plate. She swallowed the bite of steak and her small throat bobbed.
"Can I... really?" Lia whispered.
She looked at him as if he might suddenly laugh and tell her it was a cruel joke but Silas didn’t laugh.
He looked at the faded scar stretching across her ribs beneath the oversized t-shirt.
"Of course," Silas answered simply. "You have the clothes for it now, and I have the credits. I’ll get the paperwork filed tomorrow."

Silas cut into his own steak, chewing quietly as he watched her inhale her food like a starving wolf pup.
He took a sip of his water.
He set the glass down, resting his forearms on the table.
Silas looked directly at his sister.
"So, Lia," Silas asked with his deep voice cutting smoothly through the quiet kitchen.
Lia paused, a piece of steak halfway to her mouth.
She looked across the table at him as her dark eyes were wide and curious.
Silas rested his chin on his folded hands, his golden-ringed eyes locking onto hers.
"Are you still interested in heading to school?"
School.
It was something she had always wanted.

Ever since Silas had pulled her out of that freezing rotting dumpster in the lower wards, she had watched the clean, well-dressed children walk past the alleyways in their pristine uniforms, carrying heavy textbooks and glowing datapads.
They were learning about history, magic theory, and global economics, while she was learning how to pickpocket distracted tourists just to afford synthetic nutrient paste.
She had wanted to go so badly.
And Silas was well aware of it.
Before she had run away, before the guilt of being a financial burden had driven her into the dark, Silas had a plan.

His original goal had been quite simple: he would finish his brutal, grinding curriculum at the Valoria Academy, graduate with a baseline placement, and use his entry-level salary to put her in a decent preparatory section fitting of her age.
He wanted her to learn.
He wanted her to understand the complex mechanics of the world in case she was lucky enough to awaken a core and become a Lord herself.

He banked on the fact that if he became a registered Lord... even a lowly Red Core, he would be granted priority placement for his dependents but then she stole his money and vanished, and the plan had died.
Until now...
Lia slowly lowered her fork with the heavy metal clinking against the plate.
She swallowed the bite of steak and her small throat bobbed.
"Can I... really?" Lia whispered.
She looked at him as if he might suddenly laugh and tell her it was a cruel joke but Silas didn’t laugh.
He looked at the faded scar stretching across her ribs beneath the oversized t-shirt.
"Of course," Silas answered simply.
"You have the clothes for it now, and I have the credits.
I’ll get the paperwork filed tomorrow."

chapters.title: Chapter 148: Eluned Vs. Morwenna, A Battle Of Hands
paragraphs: Lia let out a genuine gasp.
"Huh?"
The last remnants of her walls completely shattered.
She didn’t finish her steak.
She scrambled out of her wooden chair, practically launching herself across the small kitchen as she threw her small arms around his muscular neck, burying her face into his shoulder.
"Thank you!" Lia cried out, her voice thick with happy overwhelming tears.
She pulled back slightly, grabbed his face with both hands, and aggressively kissed his cheek three times in rapid succession. "I love you very much, Big Brother! Mwah! Mwah! Mwah!"
"Alright, alright, that’s enough," Silas laughed loudly, reaching up and peeling her small, sticky hands off his face. "You’re getting grease on my shirt."
He gently set her back down on her feet. Lia was practically vibrating with excitement, her dark eyes shining with pure joy.
They finished their massive dinner in a state of domestic peace.
Silas cleaned the plates while Lia chattered endlessly about what kind of notebooks she wanted to buy and whether or not the academy would let her wear her new spider-silk jacket to class.
’She’s still as I remember... it would have been much better if we weren’t from the slums...’
They moved to the living room.
Silas dropped onto the expensive leather couch, turning on the massive, flat-screen television mounted on the wall.
He flipped the channel to a mindless, brightly colored Valoria City entertainment broadcast.
Lia immediately climbed up onto the couch next to him.
She didn’t sit on the other cushion. She curled up directly against his side, resting her head on his broad shoulder, completely exhausted by the emotional and physical whiplash of the day.
Within ten minutes, the soft hum of the television and the warm security of her brother’s presence completely knocked her out.
Silas looked down at her. She was fast asleep with a contented smile on her lips.
He chuckled softly, reaching out to gently pull the oversized gray t-shirt down over her knees.
"It’s just like those times..." Silas muttered quietly to himself, a wave of nostalgia hitting his chest.
He reached over, grabbing the remote off the glass coffee table, and turned off the TV.
The living room plunged into a soft, quiet darkness, illuminated only by the faint glow of the neon city lights bleeding through the rain-streaked window.
Silas stood up slowly, ensuring he didn’t wake her.
He walked over to the front door of the apartment.
He placed his hand flat against the sleek metal panel of the Spirit Lock.
He didn’t just re-engage the baseline security; he channeled a fraction of his own dense mana directly into the locking matrix.
The runic mechanisms glowed a brilliant gold, completely shutting anything from being able to enter the house without triggering an explosive backlash.
"I don’t have any other relatives so it should be good."
He walked back over to the couch.
Lia was muttering softly in her sleep.
"...new boots... don’t want the pink bow... stupid..."
Silas smiled, shaking his head. He reached down and scooped her up with one hand, effortlessly carrying her lightweight eleven-year-old frame over his shoulder.
He walked upstairs to his own master bedroom, gently laying her down directly in the center of his massive, comfortable bed.
He pulled the thick, heavy duvet up over her shoulders, tucking her in.
Silas stepped back, looking down at her.
He didn’t want her waking up in the morning wearing a greasy oversized t-shirt.

’Plus I have to time it properly so I come back when she’s awake at the very least.’ Silas thought, he would be talking with the Principal tomorrow... He had gotten into Valeria Academy on scholarship.
But for her, he was going to pay it... She was at least more happier about wanting to go to school than when he was her age.

’I remember I thought I could make it by posting one song from back on Earth.’ Silas thought, it was still on the internet in this world like this and there was no chance of that thing becoming famous. ’Right?’
Silas mentally accessed his Lord Inventory.
In a flash of golden pixelated light, the sleek dark canvas duffel bag from Weaver’s Spire materialized in his hand.
He unzipped the bag, pulling out the heavy, pristine winter sleepwear he had purchased, and set it neatly on the edge of the mattress for her.
He left the heavy duffel bag on the ground near the closet.
He walked around to the other side of the bed, kicking off his heavy combat boots. He climbed onto the mattress, lying down on his back with a heavy groan, staring up at the dark ceiling.
"What a day..." Silas sighed, rubbing the bridge of his nose.
Lia shifted in her sleep, rolling over and burying her face into his side.
"Big brother..." she mumbled into his ribs.
Silas almost melted away as he reached over, gently patting the crown of her messy brown hair.
"Don’t worry," Silas whispered into the quiet room with his golden-ringed eyes hardening in determination. "I’ll do my best."
He closed his eyes.
He didn’t have time to sleep.
He had a territory to run, a Grand Archive to build, and a Secret Realm raid to prepare for...
’I need to have the talk with the girls after all...’
Silas pulled up his glowing blue Lord interface in the darkness behind his eyelids.
He navigated past the inventory and the stat screens, locking onto the pulsing icon at the very top of the menu.
He tapped the [Descend] button.
Immediately, the world around him grew pitch black.
The physical sensation of the soft mattress and the cool, climate-controlled air of the Silverleaf apartment violently dissolved.
He was pulled into the rushing, pixelated vortex of the planar transit, his consciousness ripping through the fabric of the human world and plunging directly into the Sovereign Realm once again.
The transition ended with the familiar sensation of dense magical gravity returning to his limbs.
Silas opened his eyes.
He was standing perfectly still in the center of his private master bedchamber inside the Keep of the Blessed Land.
He looked around the room.
It was completely empty.
"Well, that’s an improvement..." Silas muttered dryly.

The last time he had ascended back to Earth and returned to his chamber, he had walked in on Kaelia, his painfully shy and fiercely loyal master chef, having a highly private intense personal moment on his bed while clutching his bedsheets.
He had expected to find at least Eluned or Morwenna lurking in his room, but the Keep was surprisingly quiet.
Silas rolled his shoulders, feeling the power of his Mythic Gold Core rapidly acclimating back to the highly saturated environment of the Umbral Basin.
He walked out of the master suite with his boots clicking rhythmically against the stone floor.

’I bought their gifts and since they’re being so calm... these girls most certainly deserve a whole lot more than that.’ Silas thought as he descended the wide, spiraling staircase heading toward the main ground floor.
"I’m hom—" Silas started to announce as he reached the bottom of the stairs.
He stopped completely dead in his tracks as the dining hall was a war zone.
Standing on opposite sides of the massive oak dining table were Eluned and Morwenna.
The two SSS-rank entities weren’t arguing about culinary techniques anymore. They were engaged in a violent terrifying contest of raw physical dominance.
They were arm wrestling!
Morwenna had her right elbow planted firmly on the oak wood.
The Dread Queen of the Astral Seas had stripped off her leather combat vest entirely, wearing only a tight sweat-soaked linen wrap around her chest.
Her massive scarred bicep was visibly bulging, the dense corded muscle straining against the skin as she gripped Eluned’s hand with terrifying bone-crushing force.
Eluned was not backing down.
The Goddess of Nature had hitched the flowing skirts of her elegant green silk dress up to her thighs, planting her boots wide on the slate floor for leverage.
Her delicate pale arm was locked against the pirate’s with her own pristine divinely forged muscles bunching and flexing with shocking brutal power.
"Put your back into it, trench-rat!" Eluned shrieked, her silver hair whipping around her face as she pushed against the pirate’s grip.
"I’m going to snap your wrist, weed!" Morwenna roared back, her stormy gray eyes burning with competitive fury.
Standing right between them, at the head of the table, was Kaelia.
The shy, easily intimidated master chef who was supposed to be the voice of reason and de-escalate conflicts while Silas was away, was completely abandoning her duties.
Instead of stopping them, Kaelia was jumping up and down, waving a wooden spoon in the air, her face flushed with adrenaline.
"Push! Push!" Kaelia cheered, completely hyping them on. "Break her guard, Morwenna! No, wait, use your leverage, Eluned!"
Silas stood in the archway, his eye twitching.
’I leave them alone for two hours...’ Silas thought, rubbing the bridge of his nose. ’Two hours.’
Morwenna let out a deafening roar.

She violently changed her footing with her heavy boots cracking the slate tiles beneath her. She flexed her massive bicep, her physical strength spiking astronomically, and aggressively slammed Eluned’s hand downward toward the oak table.
It looked like a guaranteed victory.
However, before Eluned’s knuckles could even graze the wood, the Goddess’s glowing green eyes flared with blinding divine light.
Eluned didn’t just resist the push... she strengthened her own muscles using raw, concentrated nature mana, increasing her physical density tenfold.
She dug her heels into the floor, her delicate jaw clenching, and immediately countered the momentum.

With a terrifying high-pitched scream of effort, Eluned violently reversed the leverage, driving Morwenna’s arm backward and aggressively slamming the pirate’s hand directly down onto the center of the heavy oak table.
BOOM!
The impact wasn’t just loud... it was an apocalyptic detonation.
The unrestrained physical force of an SSS-rank Goddess slamming an SSS-rank Pirate through a solid object generated a massive visible shockwave of compressed air.
The shockwave exploded outward from the point of impact. It ripped across the dining hall with terrifying velocity.
CRASH! CRASH! CRASH!
Every single heavy glass window lining the walls of the Keep instantly shattered into a million pieces, raining shrapnel down onto the courtyard outside.
The massive ironwood dining table...a piece of furniture designed to withstand a whole lot of weight instantly buckled under the pressure.
The wood splintered, groaned, and then completely vaporized, turning into a cloud of fine gray ash that rained down onto the floorboards.
Morwenna and Eluned were left standing awkwardly in the center of the room with their hands still locked together over a table that no longer existed.
Eluned didn’t care about the structural damage though. She ripped her hand free, throwing her head back and pumping her delicate fist high into the air in undeniable triumph.

"I won!" Eluned declared at the top of her lungs, her chest heaving with exertion. She looked down at the stunned pirate with a devastatingly smug sneer breaking across her flawless face. "How does Thora say it? Suck my titties, you pirate!"
Morwenna was quite shocked.
She stared at her empty hand, completely baffled that she had just been overpowered in a contest of raw strength by a woman who grew flowers for a living...
Then, the absurdity of Eluned using a dwarven insult hit her. Morwenna’s shock vanished, replaced by a loud barking snicker of genuine amusement.
"Alright, alright, you win this round, houseplant," Morwenna laughed, rubbing her sore wrist.
As the dust began to settle, the Keep’s automated high-tier restorative wards immediately activated.
The shattered glass in the window frames reversed course, flying backward and perfectly repairing themselves.
The pile of gray ash on the floor swirled upward, rapidly reconstructing the heavy oak dining table as if it had never been destroyed.
The room fell completely silent.
Silas utilized a fractional burst of his Gold Core’s velocity, completely displacing the air.
He appeared like a massive terrifying shadow directly behind Eluned.
Silas stood there, towering over the Goddess with his broad shoulders blocking out the light of the hearth.
His golden-ringed eyes were glowing fiercely in the dim room, radiating an unamused pressure that instantly froze the air in their lungs.
He looked down at her.
"What do you have to say for yourself, Elu?" Silas asked, his deep voice becoming a dangerously calm rumble that sent a violent shiver straight down her spine.
Eluned froze completely.
The triumphant arrogant smirk vanished from her face instantly. She slowly turned her head, looking up at the terrifying, glowing eyes of her Lord.
Morwenna, seeing the absolute terror on her rival’s face, immediately burst into loud obnoxious snickering, stepping back from the restored table to enjoy the execution.
Eluned swallowed incredibly hard. She frantically tried to fix her disheveled green silk dress, her cheeks burning a brilliant violently hot shade of crimson.
"Uh..." Eluned stammered, her divine composure entirely shattered as she offered a weak guilty smile. "Uh... Welcome back, my Lord."
